...the meaning of "By those who range themselves in ranks, / and those who drive away with a driving, / and those who recite a reminder" [al-Saffat: 1-3]. They said: "Those who range themselves in ranks" are the angels, who are arranged in rows. Saff (rank) is the harmonious alignment of a group in such a way that no individual deviates from another; a saff does not merely mean gathering, but gathering in harmony and discipline...

The saff is a sign of order, commitment and readiness to receive commands, and in this way the angels are arranged in rows awaiting orders, so that each of them may carry out his task and role...

As for "and those who recite a reminder" [al-Saffat: 3], they said: these are those who bring down the revelation to the messengers, because they recite it to them after they have come down with it from Allah.

Others understood "those who range themselves in ranks" [al-Saffat: 1] in another sense, from which other meanings branch out for "those who drive away with a driving" and "those who recite a reminder." They said: the meaning of "those who range themselves in ranks" [al-Saffat: 1] is the believers who line up for prayer, because prayer is the pillar of religion and a symbol of unity and togetherness, and part of its perfection is that the rows be straight...

So when we straighten the rows and stand in them, upright before Allah, the Exalted, we enter the prayer and say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," and this is a driving away of Satan. Therefore He said: "By those who range themselves in ranks, / and those who drive away with a driving" [al-Saffat: 1-2]. The meaning of "and those who recite a reminder" [al-Saffat: 3] is what we then recite of the speech of Allah: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, / the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, / Master of the Day of Judgment" [al-Fatihah: 2-4].

This is the oath. So what is the thing sworn to? The thing sworn to is His, glorified is He, saying: "Indeed, your God is One" [al-Saffat: 4]. Although this statement is the answer to an oath, Allah emphasized it first with "inna" (indeed), then emphasized it again with the lam in "la-wahid" (surely one), because it represents the foundation of the religion and the essence of the creed. The true God is One, the one who dominates all of this. We have said that wahid is not the same as ahad: wahid means He has no second like Him, whereas ahad means He is not composed of parts in His make-up; He, glorified is He, is ahad in His essence.

This form of expression is called the oath form (uslub al-qasam). Allah, exalted is He, is the One who swears, swearing that ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ [As-Saffat: 4]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us of His purpose in the oath. So Allah wants us, if we swear, not to swear except by Him, glory be to Him. But by induction (istiqra') we see that the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by some of His creation: He swears by the angels, He swears by animals, He swears by the mountains, He swears by the dawn, etc.

They said: Because Allah, exalted is He, swears by whatever He wills, on whomever He wills, whereas you do not swear except by Allah, because an oath is an exaltation of the thing sworn by, and it should not be that anything is exalted in the believer's heart except Allah. It is not correct that you say, "By the life of so-and-so, and the head of so-and-so." If you are taking an oath, then swear by Allah, as came in the noble hadith. Therefore, when something appears whose outward form is an oath by other than Allah, know that it is not considered an oath, especially if it comes from a scholar or one who is certain, such as saying, "By your father's life, O so-and-so, do such-and-such," this is not an oath; rather, it is a request (musa'alah). An oath is that you swear to something, whether it happened or not; requesting something is called musa'alah. Allah, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills, on whomever He wills, and you do not swear except by Allah; because a thing may seem trivial in your view, but it is great in the sight of its Creator, and it has a function that you overlook. When Allah swears by it, He is only drawing your attention to its importance and its role. For example, when revelation paused from our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the disbelievers did not pay attention to the wisdom in that.

The wisdom is that revelation was heavy upon the Messenger of Allah, to the point that it exhausted him, and his forehead would drip with sweat, and if revelation descended upon him while he was on a riding animal, it would groan and kneel with him; that is because revelation is heavy.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 5].

So the pause in revelation came as a mercy to the Messenger of Allah, a consolation to him, and a lightening of his suffering, and then so that he would yearn for revelation and it would return to him anew. The disbelievers did not pay attention to this, and they said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," meaning: He has left him, abandoned him, and shunned him. The contradiction in this saying is clear: at the time of faith they deny Muhammad and the Lord of Muhammad, and at the time of estrangement they say, "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," admitting that he has a lord!!

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to clarify this matter for them, and to expose their foolishness, with this oath that came fitting to the situation, carrying a gentle hint at the relationship between the thing sworn by and the thing sworn about. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it becomes still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1-5].

The meaning: O Muhammad, you were exhausted by revelation, and you had to rest so that your soul would yearn for it and seek it. When you are at ease, that will lighten your hardship in receiving it, you will taste its sweetness anew, and it will become easier and lighter for you. The Truth, glory be to Him, brought this oath with something existing and observed, on which no two people disagree.

They know ﴿the morning brightness﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1] when the sun rises and illumines the cosmos, and they know ﴿and by the night when it becomes still﴾ [Ad-Duha: 2], meaning: it grows calm and quiet. The indication here is that when the morning brightness comes and is then followed by the night with its stillness, does this mean that the morning brightness will never return?

No, rather the morning will come again after you have rested from the fatigue of the day and the striving in it, and you have restored your energy for a new day. The meaning of ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [Ad-Duha: 4] is: the return of revelation a second time will be sweeter than the first, and lighter and easier.

So then: the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills of His creatures, to teach us that these things are great in the sight of their Creator, but we have been heedless of the aspect of their greatness. He swears by whatever He wills of His creatures in order to bring closer to us, through the known, something unknown.

Here He, exalted is He, says: ﴿By those [angels] who line up in rows﴾ [As-Saffat: 1]. The "wa" is called the wa of the oath, like the "ta" and the "ba." We say: wallahi, billahi, tallahi. They said: because negating the oath here is stronger than an affirmed oath; because an oath comes only to affirm the thing sworn about, and the meaning of "I swear not" is that this is a matter clear enough that it needs no oath. The oath comes to affirm a denied or doubted matter; but this matter is manifest and evident, and yet I will swear to you.

If you survey the root (ṣ-f-f) in the Noble Qur'an, you will find it revolves around this meaning. What holds it up so that it does not fall? The Most Merciful holds it up. So he threw away the date, thought it too slow to chew, and hastened to the battlefield.

What is muhkam in the speech of Allah they adhere to, and what is mutashabih they should not declare one another disbelievers over.

The meaning of ﴿and those who recite a reminder﴾ [As-Saffat: 3] is: what we recite afterward of the words of Allah: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 2-4].

This is the oath; what is the thing sworn about? The thing sworn about is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ [As-Saffat: 4]. Although this phrase is the answer to an oath, Allah, exalted is He, emphasized it first with "inna" and then emphasized it with the lam in "lawahid," because it represents the foundation of the religion and the essence of the creed; the true God is One, the Dominator over all of this. We have said: "wahid" is not "ahad." "Wahid" means that He has no second like Him; "ahad" means that He is not composed of parts in His constitution, so He, glory be to Him, is "ahad" in His essence.

This form of expression is called the oath form (uslub al-qasam). Allah, exalted is He, is the One who swears, swearing that ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ [As-Saffat: 4]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us of His purpose in the oath. So Allah wants us, if we swear, not to swear except by Him, glory be to Him. But by induction (istiqra') we see that the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by some of His creation: He swears by the angels, He swears by animals, He swears by the mountains, He swears by the dawn, etc.

They said: Because Allah, exalted is He, swears by whatever He wills, on whomever He wills, whereas you do not swear except by Allah, because an oath is an exaltation of the thing sworn by, and it should not be that anything is exalted in the believer's heart except Allah. It is not correct that you say, "By the life of so-and-so, and the head of so-and-so." If you are taking an oath, then swear by Allah, as came in the noble hadith. Therefore, when something appears whose outward form is an oath by other than Allah, know that it is not considered an oath, especially if it comes from a scholar or one who is certain, such as saying, "By your father's life, O so-and-so, do such-and-such," this is not an oath; rather, it is a request (musa'alah). An oath is that you swear to something, whether it happened or not; requesting something is called musa'alah. Likewise the Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿...Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [An-Nisa': 1], meaning: and by the wombs, in the reading of those who put the wombs in the genitive (jarr).

Allah, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills, on whomever He wills, and you do not swear except by Allah; because a thing may seem trivial in your view, but it is great in the sight of its Creator, and it has a function that you overlook. When Allah swears by it, He is only drawing your attention to its importance and its role. For example, when revelation paused from our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the disbelievers did not pay attention to the wisdom in that.

The wisdom is that revelation was heavy upon the Messenger of Allah, to the point that it exhausted him, and his forehead would drip with sweat, and if revelation descended upon him while he was on a riding animal, it would groan and kneel with him; that is because revelation is heavy.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 5].

So the pause in revelation came as a mercy to the Messenger of Allah, a consolation to him, and a lightening of his suffering, and then so that he would yearn for revelation and it would return to him anew. The disbelievers did not pay attention to this, and they said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," meaning: He has left him, abandoned him, and shunned him. The contradiction in this saying is clear: at the time of faith they deny Muhammad and the Lord of Muhammad, and at the time of estrangement they say, "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him," admitting that he has a lord!!

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to clarify this matter for them, and to expose their foolishness, with this oath that came fitting to the situation, carrying a gentle hint at the relationship between the thing sworn by and the thing sworn about. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it becomes still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1-5].

The meaning: O Muhammad, you were exhausted by revelation, and you had to rest so that your soul would yearn for it and seek it. When you are at ease, that will lighten your hardship in receiving it, you will taste its sweetness anew, and it will become easier and lighter for you. The Truth, glory be to Him, brought this oath with something existing and observed, on which no two people disagree.

They know ﴿the morning brightness﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1] when the sun rises and illumines the cosmos, and they know ﴿and by the night when it becomes still﴾ [Ad-Duha: 2], meaning: it grows calm and quiet. The indication here is that when the morning brightness comes and is then followed by the night with its stillness, does this mean that the morning brightness will never return?

No, rather the morning will come again after you have rested from the fatigue of the day and the striving in it, and you have restored your energy for a new day. The meaning of ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [Ad-Duha: 4] is: the return of revelation a second time will be sweeter than the first, and lighter and easier.

So then: the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills of His creatures, to teach us that these things are great in the sight of their Creator, but we have been heedless of the aspect of their greatness. He swears by whatever He wills of His creatures in order to bring closer to us, through the known, something unknown.

Here He, exalted is He, says: ﴿By those [angels] who line up in rows﴾ [As-Saffat: 1]. The "wa" is called the wa of the oath, like the "ta" and the "ba." We say: wallahi, billahi, tallahi. The particles of oath may be dispensed with, and it is deduced by the lam in the answer of the oath, as in: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 3]. You do not swear about something at the outset; rather, you swear if the addressee denies it, to affirm the report for him, and the oath and emphasis come in proportion to the denial.

So if the Truth, glory be to Him, says, for example: ﴿I swear not by the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 1], or: ﴿I swear not by this city, and you are a resident of this city, and by the begetter and what he begot, We have certainly created man in hardship﴾ [Al-Balad: 1-4], and in: ﴿So I swear not by the setting-places of the stars, and indeed it is an oath, were you to know, a great one﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 75-76].

In these verses there is an oath, as evidenced by its having an answer. But why did the Qur'an negate it, saying "I swear not"? They said: because negating the oath here is stronger than an affirmed oath; because an oath comes only to affirm the thing sworn about, and the meaning of "I swear not" is that this is a matter clear enough that it needs no oath. The oath comes to affirm a denied or doubted matter; but this matter is manifest and evident, and yet I will swear to you.

As for the meaning of ﴿By those [angels] who line up in rows, and those who drive away with a driving, and those who recite a reminder﴾ [As-Saffat: 1-3]: they said: "those who line up in rows" are the angels who are arranged in rows, and "saff" is the harmonious alignment of a group such that no individual deviates from another; so "saff" does not merely mean gathering, but gathering in harmony and discipline. The row is evidence of order, commitment, and readiness to receive commands, and thus the angels are arranged awaiting orders, so that each of them may carry out his task and role.

If you survey the root (ṣ-f-f) in the Noble Qur'an, you will find it revolves around this meaning. Among that is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So gather your plan, then come in a row﴾ [Ta-Ha: 64], meaning: gathered together and united. And He said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angel, row upon row﴾ [Al-Fajr: 22].

And He said: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ [Al-Mulk: 19].

Correct: you see the bird in the sky spreading its wings like this without moving them, and yet it does not fall; likewise you see it fold its wings and still remain steady in its place. What holds it up so that it does not fall? The Most Merciful holds it up. It is as if in the holding up of the bird that we see and observe is a proof of the truth of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41].

So: the holding of the bird is a model for the holding of the heavens, except that this holding is temporary, and that one is permanent.

He says about the angels in general: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up﴾ [As-Saffat: 165], meaning: we stand in discipline awaiting orders. The "saff" here indicates harmony, and that no one exalts himself over another, and it indicates the awe of one before whom you stand in rows.

Among that also is His saying, exalted is He, regarding the bliss of Paradise: ﴿And cushions arranged in rows﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 15].

Some scholars hold that "as-saffat" has a broader meaning, referring to the sphere of spreading the call and its propagation, defending it, and protecting freedom of choice in Islam, and in fighting. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾ [As-Saff: 4]. The meaning of ﴿in His cause﴾ [As-Saff: 4] is: for the sake of making His religion known and defending it against its enemies. Making the religion known is the task of the scholars, and defending it is the task of the soldiers on the battlefield; and these and those should be one row, as if they were a solid structure. Therefore He said: ﴿Why should not a group from every community of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 122].

The scholar does not fight, because his task is to carry the call, while the fighter dies for it and sacrifices his life for it; and this sacrifice is what establishes the truthfulness of the call, for if the call were not truthful in the heart of its bearer, he would not sacrifice for it; then his sacrifice of his soul is evidence of his certainty that he is going to something better than what he is in.

You know the story of the Companion who heard the words of the Messenger of Allah about the reward of the martyr, and there was a date in his mouth that he was chewing. He said to the Messenger of Allah: "Is there anything between me and Paradise except that I fight these people until they kill me?" He said: "Yes." So he threw away the date, thought it too slow to chew, and hastened to the battlefield.

So: fighting in the cause of Allah is either with the tongue or with the sword. It must be known that the fighter who bears the sword does not bear it to compel the non-believer to faith, for there is no compulsion in religion; rather he bears it to protect his own freedom and choice in this religion, as evidenced by the fact that Islam opened many lands, and they remained upon their religion.

The single row is not only for the fighters on the battlefield, but also for the bearers of the call. It is obligatory upon those scholars that they be, in their call, a single row that disagreement does not split. What is muhkam in the speech of Allah they adhere to, and what is mutashabih they should not declare one another disbelievers over.

﴿Then those who drive away with a driving﴾ [As-Saffat: 2]: they said: this is the task of the angels, to drive away the devils who eavesdrop, as He said: ﴿And we used to sit in it in places for listening; but whoever listens now finds a watching flame awaiting him﴾ [Al-Jinn: 9].

Before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), the devils used to ascend into the sky and eavesdrop on news; Allah would permit them some of the news and commands, and they would hear them and convey them to their human allies, adding false things to them and telling people as if they knew the unseen. When the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission came, they were prevented from eavesdropping, and Allah sent meteors upon them that pursue them and burn them.

If you say: how, when we see the stars in their multitude, they remain the same and do not diminish? We say: because among the stars are stars for adornment, and among them are stars for stoning, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars, and as protection from every rebellious devil. They cannot listen to the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side, repelled, and for them is a perpetual punishment﴾ [As-Saffat: 6-9].

As for ﴿and those who recite a reminder﴾ [As-Saffat: 3]: they said: these are those who bring down revelation upon the messengers, because they recite it to them after having received it from Allah.

Others understood ﴿And those [angels] who line up﴾ [As-Saffat: 1] in another sense, from which other meanings branch off for "those who drive away with a driving" and "those who recite a reminder." They said: the meaning of ﴿And those who line up﴾ [As-Saffat: 1] is: the believers who line up for prayer, because it is the pillar of the religion and a symbol of gathering and unity, and part of its completeness is that they be in straight rows.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: and he said: "Straightening the rows in prayer is evidence of discipline, that no one deviates from another, and evidence of submission and standing in good manners before Allah." So: just as the angels are arranged in rows, you too are arranged, and each has his prayer and worship.

When we straighten the rows and stand straight in them for Allah, the Exalted, and we enter the prayer and say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," this is a driving away of Satan; therefore He said: ﴿By those [angels] who line up in rows, and those who drive away with a driving﴾ [As-Saffat: 1-2]. The meaning of ﴿and those who recite a reminder﴾ [As-Saffat: 3] is: what we recite afterward of the words of Allah: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 2-4].

This is the oath; what is the thing sworn about? The thing sworn about is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ [As-Saffat: 4]. Although this phrase is the answer to an oath, Allah, exalted is He, emphasized it first with "inna" and then emphasized it with the lam in "lawahid," because it represents the foundation of the religion and the essence of the creed; the true God is One, the Dominator over all of this. We have said: "wahid" is not "ahad." "Wahid" means that He has no second like Him; "ahad" means that He is not composed of parts in His constitution, so He, glory be to Him, is "ahad" in His essence.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verse 5:

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾

And in another verse he said:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 6] And this that is beneath the soil is what requires from us research, so that we may reach it, discover it, and bring it out, as we said, from the world of the malakut (the unseen dominion) to the world of the mulk (the visible dominion).

Here He said: ﴿and Lord of the easts﴾ [as-Saffat: 5], and in another place He said:

﴿By the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 40]. So: the Real, glorified is He, leaves room for the mind's quick grasp from the words, for as long as there are easts, there must necessarily be wests corresponding to them, because the sun does not rise upon one people except that it sets for others. So we know the wests by necessary implication.

When we survey these two words in the Book of God, we find that they come once in the singular form:

﴿Lord of the east and the west﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9], and come in the dual form:

﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [ar-Rahman: 17], and come in the plural form:

﴿By the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 40].

That is because when a single person in a single place is addressed, He says "the east and the west," since every place has an east and a west. If the places multiply, the easts and wests multiply. For example, we in a single country observe that the west of Cairo is not the west of Alexandria. When we look at all the places on the earthly sphere, we know that the easts and wests are without end, for in every half-second there is an east and a west.

Therefore we have said: among the wisdom of the Creator, glorified is He, in the rotation of the earth around its own axis and around the sun, is that He distributes the necessities of life throughout the whole cosmos. For if the sun remained facing one place, it would burn, and if it remained absent from a place, it would freeze. As a result of this movement, the Real, glorified is He, remains worshipped at every moment with every form of worship, just as we previously explained that at a single instant the dawn prayer is being performed by one people, the noon prayer by others, the afternoon prayer by others, and the sunset and night prayers, and so on throughout the day and night.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [ar-Rahman: 17], they said: "The two easts" means the east and the west, or the east of summer and the east of winter.

Yes, when we look at the sky at night we find it adorned with shining stars, and in these stars are wonders and secrets that the unlettered Arab knew. He knew the star, its name, its position and its movement, and he was guided by it in his journeys across the desert, as Allah the Glorified said: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16].

When you contemplate these stars in the sky, you see that Allah the Exalted wished to spare us the heat of the sun and leave us traces of light by which we are guided at night, because these stars only draw their light from the light of the sun.

Then the stars have another function: ﴿And as a guard against every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Saffat: 7], meaning: these stars protect us from the devils, for they pounce upon the devils and burn them. This type they call meteorites (nayazik), whereas the adornment of the stars remains, since it has no connection with this matter. As for the stars assigned to the rebellious devil, they must diminish.

The meaning of (marid) is one who rebels against the method of his Lord, for he is an heir to Iblis, taking toward his descendants the same stance that Iblis took toward Adam. If you say: Allah wants His method to prevail over the universe, so that peace, security and tranquility may prevail, then why does He create the rebellious devil? We say: so that faith may be attained in the believing soul in the presence of the opponent; otherwise what is the merit if everyone were believing and obedient? Thus we must purify the people of faith and test them, so that we may know the steadfast, for they will bear a call whose summons will continue until the Hour arises, and this is not borne except by the possessors of resolve.

As for His saying: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side﴾ [al-Saffat: 8], these verses came after Allah swore by those who drive with a driving [al-Saffat: 1–2], and we have said: among its meanings is that the angels drive the devils away from eavesdropping on the exalted assembly, where they used to snatch some fragments and cast them to their allies among the soothsayers, who would add to them much falsehood in order to mislead creation.

This eavesdropping was frequent before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ). When he (ﷺ) was sent, Allah prevented them from eavesdropping and set meteors upon them to drive them away and pounce upon them, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿And we used to sit in it on certain seats to listen; but whoever listens now will find for himself a watching flame﴾ [al-Jinn: 9], as an honouring of the message of Muhammad, that the intrusion of the devils should not corrupt it with anything that would spoil people's beliefs. So He said: ﴿By those who drive with a driving﴾ [al-Saffat: 2].

Among the wonders of zajr (driving) is that it comes with two meanings. The meaning of "zajartu insanan" is: I forbade a person from doing something; whereas "zajartu al-dabbah" means: I urge the animal to move on. Of this is the saying of the poet:

Woe is us, two lovers whom separation has parted; this one has a nest and that one is in a nest.

When my passion urged me toward union, I drove my steed to fly rather than walk.

And in the other meaning, a poet said:

.... it has left no place among us for affection

Indeed I forbade you from wrongdoing, but you forbade me from giving counsel.

So zajr comes with two opposite meanings.

As for the meaning of ﴿they cannot listen﴾ [al-Saffat: 8], there is a difference between sami'a and tasamma'a: sami'a means without intention on his part, whereas tasamma'a means he tried and made an effort to hear, regardless of whether he heard anything or not.

The meaning is: these devils were prevented, after his mission (ﷺ), from eavesdropping on news in the exalted assembly, and they try, but the angels drive them away and the meteors pounce upon them.

﴿And they are pelted from every side﴾ [al-Saffat: 8]. Al-qadhf is stoning in such a way that the blow penetrates. ﴿Outcast﴾ [al-Saffat: 9] means blamed and expelled; the madhur is one driven away with humiliation. ﴿And for them is a punishment, enduring﴾ [al-Saffat: 9] means lasting and unchanging. From it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And to Him belongs religion, enduringly﴾ [al-Nahl: 52], meaning perpetually. So religion is one and the same with all the messengers. The description of the punishment here as enduring is because they were prevented from carrying out their task of eavesdropping and snatching news from the exalted assembly.

Next, the stars have another function: ﴿And as a protection from every rebellious devil﴾. That is, these stars protect us from the devils, because they swoop down upon the devils and burn them. This type is called meteors (nayazik). As for the adornment of the stars, it remains, since it has no bearing on this matter. As for the stars assigned to the rebellious devil, they must diminish.

The meaning of "rebellious" (marid) is one who rebels against the method of his Lord, because he is an heir of Iblis, taking toward his descendants the same stance that Iblis took toward Adam. If you say: God, exalted is He, wants His method to prevail over the universe, so that peace, security and tranquility may prevail, then why does He create the rebellious devil? We say: so that faith may be made to arrive in the believing soul in the presence of the opponent. Otherwise, what is the distinction if everyone is a believer and obedient? Therefore, we must purify the people of faith and test them, so that we may know those who are steadfast, for they will carry a call whose summons will continue until the Hour is established, and this is not carried except by those of firm resolve (ulu al-'azm).

Meaning: after his (ﷺ) mission was sent, these devils were prevented from eavesdropping on news in the Highest Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la). They keep trying, but the angels repel them, and shooting stars (al-shuhub) swoop down upon them.

﴿And they are pelted from every side﴾

Al-qadhf (pelting) means stoning in such a way that the blow goes right through.

Dhuhuran (hurled away): meaning, they are reproached and driven off; al-madhur is one who is driven away with humiliation.

Wa lahum ʿadhabun wasib (﴿And for them is a punishment, enduring﴾): meaning, lasting and unchanging. From the same usage is His saying, ﴿And for Him is religion, enduring﴾ [an-Nahl: 52], meaning, perpetual. So the religion is one and the same with all the messengers. The description of the punishment here as enduring is because they were prevented from carrying out their task of eavesdropping and snatching news from the Exalted Assembly.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verse 10:

﴿Except one who snatches a fragment, and a piercing flame pursues him.﴾

The meaning: some of these rebellious devils will indeed be able to snatch some news, but they will not be able to escape with it and deliver it to their allies. Al-khatf (snatching) is a kind of taking possession of property without a right. Each of us has possession and ownership, and no one removes a thing from his ownership except one who takes it from him by aggression and injustice. And this aggression and injustice has many means, among them khatf, which is that a thing is taken from you by snatching, meaning quickly, yet in plain view of you, and you cannot prevent it, because the thing is beyond the reach of your hand, like a small child who snatches something from a seller and runs off with it.

If the owner of the thing is near and is able to hold on to it, and the aggressor contends with him, overpowers him and takes it, this is ghasb (usurpation). If the thing is taken without the knowledge of its owner, it is sariqah (theft). As for one who is entrusted with the property and takes from it, this is ikhtilas (embezzlement). All of these are means of acquiring the property of others without a right.

Likewise, the devil snatches some news and tries to escape with it, but far be it from him to succeed: ﴿a piercing flame pursues him﴾, meaning a star that swoops down upon him. And the meaning of thaqib (piercing) is penetrating, passing through the atmosphere, until it reaches its target in the shortest time.

If you say: why is he not prevented from eavesdropping from the outset? They say: there is a difference between being prevented from a thing altogether, and reaching it but not being able to carry it through or benefit from it. God enables him to obtain some news in fact, so he hears it, but the warding-off projectiles and meteors overtake him from every side, so that his regret is greater: regret that he tired himself and endured hardships in eavesdropping and snatching, and regret that he gained nothing from what he heard.

"Ask them": Allah's command to His Messenger ﷺ, meaning: ask them. The verb istaftā means to seek a fatwa (religious ruling); the alif, sīn and tā' in it indicate seeking. Fatwa comes from futuwwa (strength, vigour, the driving force). When a person is about to do something he wants to carry out, and does not know the path of truth and correctness in it, he goes to one who knows more than he does and asks him for a fatwa. That is, he asks him for a ruling or for strength, the force that drives him to act, as if he were weak and wished to be strengthened by another's opinion.

So it is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, entrusted them with giving the fatwa and answering themselves, because He is certain that the adversaries will find nothing but the word of truth to utter. Therefore He did not state the intended meaning as a report; He brought it as an acknowledgement and testimony from them, because a report may be true or false, whereas an acknowledgement cannot be denied by anyone. Hence they said: acknowledgement is the master of proofs.

The content of the question "Ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We created?" means: are they greater and stronger in creation than the heavens and the earth? He then did not give the answer, because it is clear, and it can only be that the creation of the heavens and the earth is stronger and greater than their creation. Therefore He said in another place: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

If you wish to demonstrate this matter, then reflect on your own creation and the creation of the heavens and the earth. The heavens and the earth, although they serve you, are longer-lived than you and more enduring; since Allah created them they have remained and not ceased. As for man, he dies as a child, dies as a youth, dies as an old man; he dies and leaves behind an estate that generations inherit.

So: they are stronger and mightier, because they were created with a lasting creation, and mightier in that they were governed by their own choice when they said: ﴿We come willingly﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

They chose to be subjected. The Exalted said: ﴿We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and man bore it; indeed he was unjust and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

We have said that there is a difference between the soul's capacity to bear the trust and its capacity to discharge it. A person may bear the trust and intend to discharge it, but he cannot guarantee himself at the time of discharge, for circumstances may change or something may arise that stands between him and its discharge. Therefore the heavens and the earth refrained from bearing the trust, and they departed from their own will in favour of the will of their Lord, and so they were subjected. So they are also free to choose, but they chose with a single word that extends over all time. As for man, he chose to be free to carry out or not carry out.

Moreover, the heavens and the earth, and what is between them, and what is in them of creatures, planets, bodies and orbits, move according to a precise and firm system that never deviates or falls behind: ﴿The sun and the moon run by reckoning, and the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [al-Rahman: 5-6].

And He said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day, and each is travelling in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

As for man, he stumbles through life, opposes the method of his Lord, and deviates from the path drawn for him. So which of them is greater in creation, more powerful in formation, and sounder in performance? These disbelievers, despite their disbelief, cannot but say: the heavens and the earth are stronger and greater than the creation of man.

An example of this is when Allah asked them: ﴿If you ask them who created them, they will surely say: Allah﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and ﴿If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], because these are all facts that cannot be denied, even by the disbelievers.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, presents to them a proof of the truth of this matter, saying: ﴿We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11]. That is: this is their origin, so where are they from the creation of the heavens and the earth? The meaning of lāzib (﴿لاَّزِبٍ﴾) is: clay that holds together, one part binding to another; it is midway between fluidity and hardness, that is, it is much like the ṣalṣāl clay that is distributed to pupils in schools. Clay is earth to which water has been added: if more water is added, the clay becomes soft and runs through your fingers; if little water is added, it dries and hardens.

For this reason the orientalists stopped at the stages of human formation and objected: of what was man created? The Qur'an says ﴿of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12], ﴿of dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], ﴿of black mud altered﴾ [al-Hijr: 33], and ﴿of ringing clay like pottery﴾ [al-Rahman: 14]. They overlooked that these are stages of one and the same thing, as we have said: water is poured on dust and it becomes clay; if this clay is left until it becomes foul or rotten, it becomes black mud altered; if it is left until it dries, it becomes ṣalṣāl.

The Truth, glorified is He, speaks here of the first creation of man: ﴿So ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We created? We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11], because Adam, peace be upon him, was created from clay, and then Hawwa' (Eve) was created after him. The Qur'an narrated to us the story of the creation of Adam, but for the creation of Hawwa' it sufficed with His saying: ﴿and from it He created its mate﴾ [al-Nisa': 1].

They said: "from it" means from the same kind of its formation, so it is valid that Hawwa' was created like Adam from clay, or was created from one of his ribs; in both cases she returns to the origin of clay, and Allah creates what He wills. We have already explained the comprehensiveness of divine power in the process of human creation, and that it encompasses all the rational possibilities of this process: Allah creates without father or mother, creates from a father without a mother, creates from a mother without a father, and a father and mother may come together and yet no offspring results.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He bestows females on whom He wills, and bestows males on whom He wills. Or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50].

So: the first man, Adam, peace be upon him, was created from clay, and his wife was created from his kind; then offspring came from Adam after he had left the state of clay and become a human being. Thus we, although we come from the lineage of a human being, return in our origin to clay. If you say: where is the claylike nature, since he has taken another form than clay, as is evident from the fact that when he bathes in water he does not dissolve as clay does and its particles fall apart?

We say: man, whether the origin or the offshoot, must be traced back to the first origin, which is clay, because man reproduces and multiplies through the sperm in the male and the ovum in the female. From where do these come? From blood, and blood is the product of nourishment, and nourishment's source is the earth and clay. So: we shall inevitably return to clay, but from clay once through an intermediary, and once without an intermediary.

The Truth, glorified is He, drew our attention to this matter in His saying: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

We did not witness the process of creation; Allah informed us of it, and so we know that man was created from clay that passed through these stages, until Allah breathed into it the soul and life stirred within it. All of this we did not witness, but we did witness death, which ends life, and it is for us to take what we witness as evidence for the truth of the unseen that Allah has told us of and we have not seen.

We know that the undoing of a thing comes in reverse to its building. Whoever demolishes a multi-storey building, for example, begins with the top floor. Likewise death comes as the reverse of life: first the soul departs. It is known that breathing the soul into man is the last stage in the stages of creation; so when the soul departs the body, the body returns to its origin, where the frame decays and the earth absorbs the water within it, then the remainder decomposes and returns to the dust from which it came.

Another point: man, who was created from clay, and whose substance is the nourishment that comes out of clay, when scientists analysed the human body they found it composed of 16 elements. The first is oxygen, then carbon, then hydrogen, then nitrogen, and so on. These are the same elements that make up the fertile agricultural soil that gives us our sustenance. This, then, is a proof of the truth of the Blessed and Exalted One in His saying: ﴿We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11].

"Bal" (بَلْ) indicates a turning away from the preceding statement and the beginning of a new one. ﴿You are amazed﴾ (عَجِبْتَ), with a fatha, means: O Muhammad. Al-'ajab (العَجَب) is the sense of wonder at something occurring contrary to its like. Among examples of this is the Exalted's saying regarding matters of belief: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28].

That is: how can disbelief arise from you after We have done this for you? This is a strange thing and a wondrous matter. That is, it has come contrary to what is expected of you.

But at what did the Prophet (ﷺ) marvel? He marvelled at their denial and their disbelief, despite the clarity of the decisive proofs for the truth of the matter of faith. We have presented them with proof after proof, yet they denied...

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and they mock﴾ (وَيَسْخَرُونَ). Mockery (al-sukhriyyah) is ridiculing something. The meaning is that you, O Muhammad, marvel at their denial and their rejection despite the clarity of the proofs, while they mock you and your amazement.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 37, verse 13:

The meaning of (bal) (بَلْ) is a turning away from the preceding speech and the beginning of new speech. (ʿajibta) (عَجِبْتَ), with a fatha, means: O Muhammad. And ʿajab ('ajab, wonder) is the astonishment at something occurring contrary to its like. Among this is the Exalted's saying regarding the articles of faith: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life..?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28].

That is: how can disbelief arise from you after We have done that for you? This is something astonishing, a strange matter. That is: it has come contrary to what is expected from you.

But at what did the Prophet ﷺ marvel? He marvelled at their denial and their disbelief, despite the clear, overwhelming evidences for the truth of the matter of faith. We presented to them proof after proof, and still they denied; therefore the Exalted said, addressing His Prophet ﷺ in another place: ﴿And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying..﴾ [al-Ra'd: 5].

That is: God agreed with Muhammad that he should marvel. The meaning: if you marvel, O Muhammad, then their saying is astonishing. But astonishment in whose sight? It is permissible that it is astonishment in the sight of the Messenger of God, and it is permissible that it is astonishment in the sight of the Exalted God. So then: does the Exalted God marvel as we marvel? They said: yes, by the evidence that in this verse there is a reading with a damma (بل عجبتُ, "bal ʿajibtu"), with the taʾ of the speaker, glorified is He, and by what has been transmitted in the noble hadith: why? Because he went out of the natural disposition of human creation, or he restrained himself and controlled himself, such that he did not do what young men do; so this is something astonishing from him, and the meaning of the Truthful, Glorified One's marvelling at this is that He finds this act astonishing, in order to recompense him with a recompense that is likewise astonishing.

We have already said: when a shared attribute exists between us and the Truthful, glorified is He, we must take it within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. Among this is the Exalted's saying: ﴿They deceive God, and He is their deceiver﴾ [al-Nisa': 142].

And His saying: ﴿And they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

Therefore beware that you say: God is a deceiver or God is a plotter; for there is a difference between the names of God, the Exalted, and the verbs by which He described Himself, glorified is He. Plotting, for example, is among the actions of humans, and it is meant as deceiving the opponent and misleading him, so that you may reach your aim from him, and this plotting is met by a like plotting that resembles it or surpasses it.

Makr (plotting) is derived from their saying "a shajara mamkurah" (شجرة ممكورة), a tree whose branches are twisted and wrapped around one another, such that you cannot distinguish it, nor return each branch in it to its root; likewise plotting contains twisting and stratagem to conceal one's evils from one's opponent. This is with regard to the plotting of humans against one another; but if God plots against you, nothing will save you from His plotting. Therefore the Glorified said: ﴿And God is the best of plotters﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they mock﴾ [al-Saffat: 12]. Mockery (al-sukhriyyah) is ridicule of a thing, and the meaning is that you marvel, O Muhammad, at their denial and their rejection despite the clear evidences, while they mock you and your marvelling. ﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾ [al-Saffat: 13], that is: with other signs and proofs that guide them, ﴿they do not remember﴾ [al-Saffat: 13], that is: they turn away from them, and do not pay attention to them, and insist on denial. ﴿And when they see a sign﴾ [al-Saffat: 14], that is: a new proof, ﴿they mock greatly﴾ [al-Saffat: 14], that is: they exaggerate in mockery.

In the verse before the previous one He said: ﴿And they mock﴾ [al-Saffat: 12], and here ﴿they mock greatly (yastaskhirun)﴾ [al-Saffat: 14]. This is evidence that among these deniers are people whose hearts are softened by the signs of God and the evidences of faith, and when their hearts are softened the impulse of scheming against Muhammad lightens in them, so they suffice with denial without mockery; for refusal comes in degrees: one refuses to do what you command him, and another refuses to do it and mocks you.

As for those who mock, they do not suffice with mocking the Messenger of God; rather ﴿yastaskhirun﴾ [al-Saffat: 14], that is: they ask those who do not mock to mock, that is: they make others mock. So then, there is a difference between yaskhurun (يسخرون) and yastaskhirun (يستسخرون), lest we say, as some orientalists say: this is repetition in the speech of God.

...In the verse before the previous one, He said: "and they mock" (Al-Saffat: 12), and here "they seek to mock" (yastaskhirun) (Al-Saffat: 14). This is evidence that among these deniers there are people whose hearts are softened by the signs of Allah and the evidences of faith. When their hearts are softened, their impulse to scheme against Muhammad (ﷺ) lessens, so they content themselves with denial without mockery, because refusal comes in degrees: one refuses to do what you command him, and another refuses to do it and mocks you.

As for those who mock, they do not content themselves with mocking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Rather, "yastaskhirun" means: they ask those who do not mock to mock, that is, they make others mock.

Meaning of "Inna hadha illa sihrun mubin" (Indeed, this is nothing but clear magic): it means, this is nothing but evident magic. Magic, as we have said, is the imagining of a thing that does not actually exist, so that it seems to you to be existing. Magic does not change the reality of a thing; it only bewitches the one who looks at it, as Allah the Exalted said about the magicians of Pharaoh: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people﴾ [al-A'raf: 116]. And He said: ﴿It was imagined to him, because of their magic, that their ropes and staffs were moving﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66].

So then: what has magic to do with the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), and with the matter of faith to which he calls the people? The answer to this slander is simple and clear: if Muhammad had the power to bewitch people so that they believed in his call, and he bewitched those who believed, then why did he not bewitch you as well? So this is a baseless accusation that has no meaning.

Strange of them is their denial of resurrection after the proofs we have set before them, even though they deny our proofs and reject them. Have they not heard from the earlier nations and the messages that passed on that resurrection is true? So then: it is obstinacy and arrogance in refusing to accept the truth.

Therefore, the Noble Qur'an sets before them an example and a proof of the truthfulness of the report of resurrection, and presents this story of the earlier nations in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Or like the one who passed by a town, while it was fallen upon its roofs. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then resurrected him. He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not spoiled. And look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 259].

This is a real story, because the Qur'an related it to us from the earlier nations, so that it would be a proof of Allah's power to resurrect the dead. It is the story of a man seeking the truth, whom Allah made an example and a model for himself first, and for those who came after him. When he passed by the town in that state of ruin, he thought it unlikely that it would live again with its people, so Allah caused him to die in order to show him how He brings the dead to life.

The man spoke truly in his saying ﴿I have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 259], and Allah spoke truly in His saying ﴿Rather, you have remained a hundred years﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 259]. How? Because the donkey's bones, which had turned to dust, indicated the hundred years, while his food, which had not changed, indicated a day or part of a day. This is not strange, since the one who acts is Allah, the Constrictor, the Expander, who alone is able to combine opposites, contracting time for some people and expanding it for others.

Did He not command His prophet Moses, peace be upon him, to strike the sea with his staff, so that the water became like a great mountain for every division, and command him to strike the rock with his staff, so that twelve springs gushed forth from it? So then: it is the absoluteness of power.

It is also strange of them that they ask about the forefathers, although the matter of resurrection is one. Their saying ﴿Or our first forefathers?﴾ [As-Saffat: 17] is evidence of their confusion; or perhaps they understood that whoever dies recently (fresh, "ṭāzah") is the one who will be resurrected, whereas the old, its resurrection is not possible.

Allah replies to them: (Say) — that is, say to them, O Muhammad, with full mouth — (Yes) — that is, you will be resurrected. The Prophet says it with the assurance of one who is certain, because he is commanded to say it by Allah, who is capable of resurrecting creation: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled"﴾ [As-Saffat: 18]. That is, you will be resurrected while you are ﴿humbled﴾ [As-Saffat: 18], meaning abased, humiliated, submissive, as a recompense for obstinacy, contention, and arrogance toward accepting the truth in this world, as Allah the Exalted said in another place: ﴿Rather, they are today submitting [in surrender]﴾ [As-Saffat: 26].

It is also strange of them that they ask about the forefathers, even though the matter of resurrection is one and the same. Their saying ﴿Or our forefathers of old?﴾ is evidence of their confusion. Perhaps they understood that only the one who has recently died would be raised, whereas the one who died long ago cannot be raised.

And Allah responds to them: "Say (qul)," meaning: say to them, O Muhammad, with your full mouth, "Yes (na'am)," meaning: you will be resurrected. The Prophet says it with the assurance of one who is certain, because he is commanded to say it by Allah, who is capable of raising up creation. ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ Meaning: you will be resurrected while you are *dakhirun*, meaning: abased, humiliated, and submissive, as a recompense for your obstinacy, contentiousness, and arrogance in rejecting the truth in the world.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 37, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then it will be but one shout (zajrah), and behold, they will be looking on.﴾ That is: the matter of resurrection (al-ba'th) is but one shout (zajrah), a single cry, or a single blast (nafkhah), sufficient to bring them out of their graves, ﴿and behold, they will be looking on.﴾ Not that We will go to each one of them and wake him up... So, the resurrection which you deny is an easy matter for Us, and it costs Us nothing.

The cry in itself does not raise the dead; rather, it is merely a permission given to the angel to begin his task. It is like the bell with which work is started. After the zajrah, ﴿behold (fa-idha), they will be looking on﴾ immediately, for here fa-idha indicates suddenness, so the matter will not take any time. And at the very first moment they rise from the graves, they will be looking "here and there" (yanzuruna), because they will see a strange matter they have never known before, and what they used to deny in the world will take them by surprise.

Then when they see this scene, they will say: "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense (yawm al-din)." "This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny."

It is they who say this, and they who call down woe and destruction upon themselves. We do not say it; it is they who say it: "Woe to us!" That is, "Come, for this is your time." Now the realities have been laid bare for them, their falsehood and the corruption of their thinking have become clear, along with the stubbornness and obstinacy they were engaged in during the world. The first thing that becomes clear to a person is the corruption of his thinking and the evil of his deeds; the first thing he does is blame himself, and so he calls down woe upon himself.

As for their saying, "This is the Day of Recompense," it means: the day of the reward for deeds. This is the recompense they did not believe in during the world, and here they now acknowledge it. Or, "This is the Day of Recompense" may mean: this is the day on which religion (din) will benefit, just as you say to your child who is about to face an examination, "This is the day of study," meaning: the day on which nothing will benefit you except your studying.

...the separation (al-fasl) can only occur in a dispute (khusumah), and the dispute here was between the messengers and their peoples who denied them and were obstinate. Such a dispute is not ended by argument (jadal), because those who deny have contentiousness (ladad) and obstinacy (inad). Nor may it be ended by the sword, since the wrongdoer may die without being requited (yaqtassa minhu).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verses 22–24:

Meaning: gather all of these together into the Fire. ﴿Those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ [al-Saffat: 22]. So, the ones gathered are three: those who did wrong, as the recompense for their wrongdoing; their spouses; and what they used to worship besides Allah.

We have said that zawj (spouse, "pair") means one individual and the like of it alongside it. So we do not say of a man and a woman together that they are a zawj; rather they are zawjan (a pair). The man is called zawj and the woman is called zawj, and not that zawj means the two together, as some suppose. The same applies to the word tawam (twin): each of the two is called tawam, and together they are tawamān (twins). For this reason Allah the Exalted said in Surat al-An'am: ﴿Eight mates: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: has He forbidden the two males or the two females...?﴾ [al-An'am: 143].

And He said: ﴿And of the camels two, and of the cattle two...﴾ [al-An'am: 144].

Had zawj been applied to two, He would have said: "four mates."

The meaning of the words ﴿and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22] is: their spouses in the world, such as a wife who helps her husband in wrongdoing, like the wife of Abu Lahab, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! His wealth and what he gained will not avail him. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾ [al-Masad: 1–5].

Or what is meant by "their spouses" is their likenesses, their counterparts, and their companions who misled them and led them astray. ﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾ [al-Saffat: 22–23], that is, the idols they worshipped besides Allah, will be gathered with them into the Fire, so that they see their gods, which they worshipped and clung to, preceding them into the Fire, and their hope of salvation is cut off. And it is a demonstration of the corruption of their thinking, in that they worshipped idols that neither harm nor benefit. This is a rebuke to them. Therefore this rebuke extends sharply in His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 23]. Is casting them into the Fire a guidance? The meaning is: direct them to the road of Hell, that is, in mockery of them and derision toward them.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24], that is, hold them back for questioning and for reckoning. This questioning will be individual, not collective: each one of them will be questioned and will be debated with. They said: in the questioning there is the soul's rebuking of itself before Allah rebukes them, those who disbelieved in Him. That is, at the moment they witness the Resurrection and the standing of reckoning, they rebuke themselves, and they regret at a time when regret will not avail.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24], that is, hold them back for questioning and for reckoning. This questioning will be individual, not collective: each one of them will be questioned and will be debated with. They said: in the questioning there is the soul's rebuking of itself before Allah rebukes them, those who disbelieved in Him. That is, at the moment they witness the Resurrection and the standing of reckoning, they rebuke themselves, and they regret at a time when regret will not avail.

This interrogation is also in the manner of mockery and derision. The meaning is: "What is the matter with you now that you do not help one another, when you used to help one another in the world?" The followers would help the leaders, and the leaders would mobilize the followers...

This interrogation is also in the manner of mockery and scorn. That is, "What is the matter with you now that you do not help one another, when in the world you used to help each other?" The followers would support the leaders, and the leaders would recruit the followers. Their situation in this standing resembles the proverb "the pot met its lid" (wafaqa shannun tabaqahu), or our saying "the unlucky one has been matched with the unlucky one" (ittalama al-mit'us ʿala khayib al-raja').

Therefore, the Exalted says after it: ﴿Rather, they this Day are submitting [to one another]﴾ [al-Saffat: 26], meaning: humbled, subdued, abased and humiliated. And we say: "He raised the white flag." That is, he no longer has any strength left with which to defend himself, nor any argument or reasoning. He is now sitting in humiliation and disgrace, awaiting the command of God concerning him.

This is a commentary by al-Sha'rawi on surah 37, verses 27–29.

Consider this confrontation between the followers and those they followed, after the disappointment of all has become evident and the realities that they denied in the world and called lies have been uncovered. Now each of them throws the responsibility onto the other, and they question one another.

﴿They will say﴾ [al-Saffat: 28], i.e., the followers: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾ [al-Saffat: 28]. Al-yamin (the right) means from the direction of the right. From the same root comes al-yaman (Yemen) and al-tayammun (seeking blessing from the right), and al-yamin is the direction of good. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded us to prefer the right in everything: by it we give the greeting of peace, by it we eat and drink, and by it we take things and write, because it is honoured and dignified. Even the Arabs of old used to take omens from the direction of the right, if a bird flew toward the right.

Al-yamin also has among its meanings that it is the source of strength in action. Most people use the right hand, and it is the stronger one for them. We have been asked once about those who work with the left hand: should we forbid them from that? We say: working with the right or the left is not merely a habit; rather it is a natural formation in the body. In the body there is a centre that controls the distribution of strength. Some people have the centre of strength inclined toward the right, so their right is stronger than their left; some are the opposite; and some have the centre of strength balanced, so they work with the right and with the left with equal strength. This is called (al-adbat (ambidextrous)), like our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Among the meanings of al-yamin is also the oath and swearing. All these meanings are intended in this verse: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right﴾ [al-Saffat: 28], meaning: from the direction of good and truth, to turn us away from it; or from the side of force and strength, to compel us to act; or by oath, meaning: you swore to us that this is the correct path and that there is no other path.

The leaders reply to the followers: ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers"﴾ [al-Saffat: 29], meaning: we did not take you out of faith into disbelief; rather you were by your very nature not believers, and as soon as we gestured to you, you went after us and followed us. ﴿And we had no authority over you﴾ [al-Saffat: 30]. Authority (sultan) is either the authority of force that overpowers you into action, or the authority of proof that persuades you into disbelief. So we had over you neither the authority of force and coercion, nor the authority of argument and persuasion.

﴿Rather, you were﴾ [al-Saffat: 30] by your own nature ﴿a people transgressing﴾ [al-Saffat: 30], i.e., exceeding the limit in disbelief and misguidance. This is the same statement that Iblis makes to his followers in the Hereafter, when he disowns them and places on them the responsibility for their disbelief, as the Noble Qur'an relates: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had over you no authority except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves"﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

Rather, you yourselves were by your own nature a people transgressing the limits, that is, exceeding all bounds in disbelief and in error. And this is the instruction of Iblis, which he speaks to his followers in the Hereafter when he disowns them and places upon them the responsibility for their disbelief...

...Consider His words, glorified is He: "Indeed, we are tasting [the punishment]" (inna la-dha'iqun), and they did not say "we are being punished" (mu'adhdhabun) or "we are being burned" (muharraqun). For punishment or burning may come to an end at some point in time, whereas tasting (al-idhaqa) is constant and continuous. This meaning is clear in His words, exalted is He:

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment﴾ [al-Nisa': 56].

And their saying: "So we misled you" (fa-aghwaynākum) means: we pointed you to the path of error and deviation. The one who is ghawi (misguided) is the one who has strayed from the path of goodness and truth. "Indeed, we were misguided" (innā kunnā ghāwīn). The meaning is: if we ourselves were misguided and astray, then why would we leave you to guidance and faith? It is necessary that you drink with us from the same cup. This is the reasoning of their teacher, Iblis (Satan). When he disobeyed and was expelled from the mercy of God, he swore that he would mislead the descendants of Adam along with him, so that they would be like him in error.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes this confrontation among the people of falsehood and establishes this reality: ﴿Indeed, they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment﴾. That is, on the Day of Resurrection. And this is Our way with the people of misguidance.

Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals (al-mujrimun). The criminal (al-mujrim) is the one who denies the first article of faith, which is monotheism (al-tawhid). Therefore, in the following verse, the Truth, glorified is He, describes them: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them...﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, they﴾ [Al-Saffat: 35], meaning the disbelievers who were described as criminals, ﴿when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," were arrogant﴾ [Al-Saffat: 35], meaning they were too proud to accept it and affirm it. ﴿And they said, "Shall we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ [Al-Saffat: 36], meaning they turn away from worshipping them, ﴿for a mad poet﴾ [Al-Saffat: 36], meaning on account of him and on account of his call.

It is strange of the Arabs, who are a people of speech. They weigh words and savour them, they establish markets and fairs for them, and they honour poetry and poets to such an extent that they hung their finest odes on the curtains of the Ka'bah. It is strange that a people in this condition should say ﴿our gods﴾ [Al-Saffat: 36] while they know full well the meaning of "gods" (alihah) and the meaning of worship. For "ilah" means "the one worshipped" (al-ma'bud). So by what right were the idols worshipped? What did [the Prophet] command you? What did he forbid you from? What method did he bring you?

Yes, they knew that these were lifeless objects that neither harm nor benefit. But they worshipped them through the innate religious disposition (fitrat al-tadayyun) in human beings. Man by nature is religious; he loves to lean on a power higher than himself, to turn to it in hardship, a power that helps him to endure and to bear events with patience. They found in these gods that they were gods without obligations and without demands, so they worshipped them besides Allah.

Then it is strange of them, being a people of speech, that they do not distinguish between the speech of Allah in the Qur'an and poetry, when they are the people most knowledgeable about it, its metres and its rhymes. Where is poetry in comparison with the speech of Allah in the Qur'an? Then it is strange of them that they accuse the Messenger of Allah of madness, when they knew him best, his character, his qualities and his conduct among them before his commission. How far madness is from one who gathered the finest qualities and noble character!

Madness is that the mad person behaves with his limbs in a way that does not pass through reason. The mad person does not discriminate between things, and does not know the harmful from the beneficial. The mad person has no character. Therefore the truth answers them and repels their accusations against His Messenger, saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed you are of a great character﴾ [Al-Qalam: 1–4].
