Consider God's words about him: ﴿when he fled to the laden ship﴾ [al-Saffat 37:140]. The meaning of *abaqa* (أبق) is "fled," but not absolute fleeing. It is the flight of a slave from his master, not his flight from his employer, nor the flight of my sons from me, for that is not called *ubuq*. The word *abaqa* carries the sense of absolute servitude to the supreme Master: God is his Master and he is His servant.

Because the slave is owned by the right of possession, he is by his very self a possession of mine when I take him captive. Indeed, by his very self. For God preserved his blood through this ownership: instead of killing him in war, I took him captive and enslaved him. He does not become a slave unless I capture him, and as long as I have captured him and have power over him, you can kill him. Therefore God gave you ownership of his neck, because He protected his blood from being spilled.

So there is no need to compare slavery with freedom. If you want a comparison, compare slavery with killing. Even if the slave himself were given the choice between living under a master who employs him and being killed, he would choose slavery. So slavery here is not a disgrace in Islam; rather it is a kindness that Islam conferred upon these slaves.

Muhammad (ﷺ) did not come to legislate for slavery or to increase the number of slaves; he came to abolish slavery and dry up its sources. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came, slavery existed in society and in abundance, for it had twenty-three sources from which slavery came. So what did Islam do?

It closed all these sources, and nothing remained of them except the captive taken in a legitimate war. Then it began to enumerate the channels of slavery and open the doors for freeing slaves, as we have seen in the expiations (*kaffarat*) and in voluntary emancipation of necks. If you have not committed a sin that calls for an expiation and the freeing of a neck, and you have no need to voluntarily free a neck, and you keep the slaves you have, then be generous to them.

The Prophet (ﷺ) laid down for us a constitution to follow in treating slaves when he said: "Thus has Islam commanded in the matter of slaves." Islam permitted slavery to continue because of legitimate war, since I have an unbelieving enemy who besieges me and fights me, and takes my children captive among them. Therefore there must be reciprocity: if they take captives from us, we take captives from them; if they ransom their captives, we ransom ours; if they release, we release… and so on. So the one who reflects on this matter will find that Muhammad (ﷺ) did not come to legislate for slavery, but to legislate for manumission.

As for God's words concerning our master Yunus, ﴿when he fled﴾ [al-Saffat 37:140], this is not a reproach against the Prophet of God Yunus, because *abaqa* means that he acknowledged he was a servant of his Lord. This episode is not detailed here; it comes in another surah, so that we know the matter is not mechanical. The matter is the wills of Truth, which come in their place for a wisdom. Our master Yunus has a surah named after him, and his name is mentioned only once, and then his whole history is mentioned in surahs other than the one named after him.

So the meaning of *abaqa* is that he fled from his master, or left his people without permission from his Lord. This matter is detailed in God's words: ﴿And Dhu'l-Nun﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87], meaning the companion of the fish, who is our master Yunus, ﴿when he went off in anger﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87]. The word *mughadiban* (مغاضباً) is not the same as *ghadiban* (غاضباً). *Mughadiban* contains the form *mufa'ala* (مفاعلة), which implies participation and mutuality: he is angry, and the one opposite him is also angry. It is like *shaarak Muhammadun 'Aliyyan* (شارك محمد علياً), "Muhammad participated with Ali," where Ali also participates with Muhammad. *Ghadib* (غاضب), by contrast, means only from his own side.

But angry at whom? The other party here is the people. When they denied him and harmed him, he could not bear it. So he was not angry at his Lord, but angry at his people, while still having hope and a presumption about his Lord, that He would forgive him for this conduct. That is why God said after it: ﴿so he thought that We would not decree (a restriction) upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87]. Some understood *naqdira* (نقدر) to mean "to have power." But far be it that the Prophet of God would think that God could not have power over him, or that He would not return him to his people.

Rather, the meaning of *naqdira* here is "We would constrict him," as in God's words: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what God has given him﴾ [al-Talaq 65:7]. So this is his confidence in the mercy of the One who sent him, and that He, glory be to Him, would not constrict him from venting his feelings when he left his people without permission from his Lord.

The meaning of *al-fulk* (الفلك) is the ship, and *al-mashhun* (المشحون) means full. This shows us that a ship has a specific load that should not be exceeded, otherwise the ship is exposed to sinking according to Archimedes' principle. By this principle objects float, and on it the idea of submarines was built. The meaning of "submarine" (*ghawwasa*) is: it dives under water, because its weight is heavier than the water it displaces. Therefore they say: "Lighter, it floats."

Since the ship was full, and the number of people exceeded the ship's load, the captain decided to throw one of the passengers overboard to lighten the load. So they cast lots, and the lot fell to our master Yunus, and they threw him into the sea, and the fish swallowed him. This is the meaning of ﴿and he cast lots﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141]: he entered the lottery with them and cast his lot with their lots. ﴿And he was among the losers﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141]. The meaning of *al-mudhadin* (المدحضين) is the one who loses in a transaction, and what is meant is the lottery, in which his share was to be thrown into the sea.

Drawing lots is a method of selection that clears the owner of the ship from being accused of partiality or favoritism. The casting of lots is a purely determined matter, in which desire has no part, and it is evidence of the justice of the judgment. That is why we often resort, when conducting a lottery, to a small child who picks the papers thrown, for example, because he cannot distinguish between them. So his choice comes as a destiny free from desire.

God's words ﴿and he cast lots﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141], meaning he entered the lottery with them, give us a social scene that spares us embarrassment and resentment. For if there is something that cannot accommodate all who seek it, it is not right for the one in charge of it to distinguish among those seekers, because favoring one over another leaves something in the soul. Conducting a lottery is a destined choice in which no one has a say.

This matter was resorted to by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) too: he removed himself from choosing and left it to God the Exalted and His destiny. The she-camel walked until she knelt at the dwellings of Banu al-Najjar.

Someone might say: Does a ship survive or sink because of one person who lightened its weight or added to it? We say: Yes. Have you not heard of the straw that broke the camel's back? When you load a camel, it carries according to its capacity, until if you add one more twig it kneels under its load. The truth is that one twig or straw does not break a camel's back; rather, the sum of the twigs and the last straw alone tipped the weight and brought it to the point of being unbearable. Likewise in the ship of our master Yunus, where its survival from sinking depended on throwing one of its passengers overboard, and the destruction of one is better than the destruction of all.

We learn from this matter that when danger befalls a group, there is no objection to one of them warding it off from them, and the lottery is what determines this one.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Saffat 37:142], meaning the fish swallowed him, and he, peace be upon him, did what deserves blame. Blame is a kind of reproach, and there is a difference between what one is blamed for and what one is punished for. Our master Yunus did what deserved reproach from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as if God were saying to him: "You hurried when you left your people and became constricted by them at the first harm you encountered, and it was incumbent upon you to be patient and bear harm in the cause of your call." So blame is a form of reproach that does not reach the level of punishment. Reproach usually arises between loved ones to preserve affection, which is why the poet said:

"As for reproach, it is most fitting among the beloved,
and love is made right by reproach and is true."

It is well known that you only reproach the one you are eager to keep in your company.

So several things intercede for our master Yunus here. The first is ﴿when he fled﴾ [al-Saffat 37:140], meaning he was a servant of God the Exalted. Then ﴿so he thought that We would not constrict him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87], meaning We would not restrict him, and this is good opinion of God. Then ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Saffat 37:142]: God reproached him and blamed him only with blame, for a matter that should not be from a prophet, and reproach is evidence of love.

As for God's words: ﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (God), he would have remained in its belly until the day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Saffat 37:143-144]. Glorification (*tasbih*, التسبيح) means the absolute declaration of God the Exalted's transcendence. His being among those who glorify made him a place of blame and reproach, not of harm and punishment. Had it not been for his faith and his glorification, he would have remained in the belly of the fish until the day they are resurrected.

Therefore God gave you ownership of his neck, because He protected his blood from being spilled.

So there is no need to compare slavery with freedom. If you want a comparison, compare slavery with killing. Even if the slave himself were given the choice between living under a master who employs him and being killed, he would choose slavery. So slavery here is not a disgrace in Islam; rather it is a kindness that Islam conferred upon these slaves.

Muhammad (ﷺ) did not come to legislate for slavery or to increase the number of slaves; he came to abolish slavery and dry up its sources. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came, slavery existed in society and in abundance, for it had twenty-three sources from which slavery came. So what did Islam do?

It closed all these sources, and nothing remained of them except the captive taken in a legitimate war. Then it began to enumerate the channels of slavery and open the doors for freeing slaves, as we have seen in the expiations (*kaffarat*) and in voluntary emancipation of necks. If you have not committed a sin that calls for an expiation and the freeing of a neck, and you have no need to voluntarily free a neck, and you keep the slaves you have, then be generous to them.

The Prophet (ﷺ) laid down for us a constitution to follow in treating slaves when he said: "Thus has Islam commanded in the matter of slaves." Islam permitted slavery to continue because of legitimate war, since I have an unbelieving enemy who besieges me and fights me, and takes my children captive among them. Therefore there must be reciprocity: if they take captives from us, we take captives from them; if they ransom their captives, we ransom ours; if they release, we release… and so on. So the one who reflects on this matter will find that Muhammad (ﷺ) did not come to legislate for slavery, but to legislate for manumission.

As for God's words concerning our master Yunus, ﴿when he fled﴾ [al-Saffat 37:140], this is not a reproach against the Prophet of God Yunus, because *abaqa* means that he acknowledged he was a servant of his Lord. This episode is not detailed here; it comes in another surah, so that we know the matter is not mechanical. The matter is the wills of Truth, which come in their place for a wisdom. Our master Yunus has a surah named after him, and his name is mentioned only once, and then his whole history is mentioned in surahs other than the one named after him.

So the meaning of *abaqa* is that he fled from his master, or left his people without permission from his Lord. This matter is detailed in God's words: ﴿And Dhu'l-Nun﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87], meaning the companion of the fish, who is our master Yunus, ﴿when he went off in anger﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87]. The word *mughadiban* (مغاضباً) is not the same as *ghadiban* (غاضباً). *Mughadiban* contains the form *mufa'ala* (مفاعلة), which implies participation and mutuality: he is angry, and the one opposite him is also angry. It is like *shaarak Muhammadun 'Aliyyan* (شارك محمد علياً), "Muhammad participated with Ali," where Ali also participates with Muhammad. *Ghadib* (غاضب), by contrast, means only from his own side.

But angry at whom? The other party here is the people. When they denied him and harmed him, he could not bear it. So he was not angry at his Lord, but angry at his people, while still having hope and a presumption about his Lord, that He would forgive him for this conduct. That is why God said after it: ﴿so he thought that We would not decree (a restriction) upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87]. Some understood *naqdira* (نقدر) to mean "to have power." But far be it that the Prophet of God would think that God could not have power over him, or that He would not return him to his people.

Rather, the meaning of *naqdira* here is "We would constrict him," as in God's words: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what God has given him﴾ [al-Talaq 65:7]. So this is his confidence in the mercy of the One who sent him, and that He, glory be to Him, would not constrict him from venting his feelings when he left his people without permission from his Lord.

The meaning of *al-fulk* (الفلك) is the ship, and *al-mashhun* (المشحون) means full. This shows us that a ship has a specific load that should not be exceeded, otherwise the ship is exposed to sinking according to Archimedes' principle. By this principle objects float, and on it the idea of submarines was built. The meaning of "submarine" (*ghawwasa*) is: it dives under water, because its weight is heavier than the water it displaces. Therefore they say: "Lighter, it floats."

Since the ship was full, and the number of people exceeded the ship's load, the captain decided to throw one of the passengers overboard to lighten the load. So they cast lots, and the lot fell to our master Yunus, and they threw him into the sea, and the fish swallowed him. This is the meaning of ﴿and he cast lots﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141]: he entered the lottery with them and cast his lot with their lots. ﴿And he was among the losers﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141]. The meaning of *al-mudhadin* (المدحضين) is the one who loses in a transaction, and what is meant is the lottery, in which his share was to be thrown into the sea.

Drawing lots is a method of selection that clears the owner of the ship from being accused of partiality or favoritism. The casting of lots is a purely determined matter, in which desire has no part, and it is evidence of the justice of the judgment. That is why we often resort, when conducting a lottery, to a small child who picks the papers thrown, for example, because he cannot distinguish between them. So his choice comes as a destiny free from desire.

God's words ﴿and he cast lots﴾ [al-Saffat 37:141], meaning he entered the lottery with them, give us a social scene that spares us embarrassment and resentment. For if there is something that cannot accommodate all who seek it, it is not right for the one in charge of it to distinguish among those seekers, because favoring one over another leaves something in the soul. Conducting a lottery is a destined choice in which no one has a say.

This matter was resorted to by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) too: he removed himself from choosing and left it to God the Exalted and His destiny. The she-camel walked until she knelt at the dwellings of Banu al-Najjar.

Someone might say: Does a ship survive or sink because of one person who lightened its weight or added to it? We say: Yes. Have you not heard of the straw that broke the camel's back? When you load a camel, it carries according to its capacity, until if you add one more twig it kneels under its load. The truth is that one twig or straw does not break a camel's back; rather, the sum of the twigs and the last straw alone tipped the weight and brought it to the point of being unbearable. Likewise in the ship of our master Yunus, where its survival from sinking depended on throwing one of its passengers overboard, and the destruction of one is better than the destruction of all.

We learn from this matter that when danger befalls a group, there is no objection to one of them warding it off from them, and the lottery is what determines this one.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Saffat 37:142], meaning the fish swallowed him, and he, peace be upon him, did what deserves blame. Blame is a kind of reproach, and there is a difference between what one is blamed for and what one is punished for. Our master Yunus did what deserved reproach from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, as if God were saying to him: "You hurried when you left your people and became constricted by them at the first harm you encountered, and it was incumbent upon you to be patient and bear harm in the cause of your call." So blame is a form of reproach that does not reach the level of punishment. Reproach usually arises between loved ones to preserve affection, which is why the poet said:

"As for reproach, it is most fitting among the beloved,
and love is made right by reproach and is true."

It is well known that you only reproach the one you are eager to keep in your company.

So several things intercede for our master Yunus here. The first is ﴿when he fled﴾ [al-Saffat 37:140], meaning he was a servant of God the Exalted. Then ﴿so he thought that We would not constrict him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:87], meaning We would not restrict him, and this is good opinion of God. Then ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Saffat 37:142]: God reproached him and blamed him only with blame, for a matter that should not be from a prophet, and reproach is evidence of love.

As for God's words: ﴿Had he not been among those who glorify (God), he would have remained in its belly until the day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Saffat 37:143-144]. Glorification (*tasbih*, التسبيح) means the absolute declaration of God the Exalted's transcendence. His being among those who glorify made him a place of blame and reproach, not of harm and punishment. Had it not been for his faith and his glorification, he would have remained in the belly of the fish until the day they are resurrected.

The matter of the Truth's, glory be to Him, reproach of His prophet Yunus for leaving his people and abandoning them, merely because they opposed and denied him, reminds us of God the Exalted's custom with His messengers, which is victory and support: ﴿Indeed We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 40:51].

But this victory may be delayed, although God is able to give them victory at the very first moment. Yet the Truth, glory be to Him, wants by that two things:

First: that corruption should spread and become general, until people are constricted by it and turn longingly toward the truth and goodness, and they themselves strive toward it.

Second: that God may test the believers in the messengers, and distinguish among them those who are steadfast and capable of bearing the hardships of the call afterward. So the delay of victory is not abandonment of the messengers, nor their forsaking, for God the Exalted would never send a messenger and then forsake him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verses 145–148:

We notice in the matter of seizure (al-akhdh) that He said, ﴿So the whale swallowed him﴾ [al-Saffat: 142], attributing the act to the whale. But here, in the matter of deliverance, He attributed the act to God, saying, ﴿So We cast him out﴾ [al-Saffat: 145], meaning: We threw him and flung him ﴿onto the open shore﴾ [al-Saffat: 145], meaning: onto a wide, open stretch of land. ﴿And he was ailing﴾ [al-Saffat: 145], meaning: he was sick, or exhausted from the distress he had suffered in the belly of the whale. Or he was ailing from brooding over what had happened with his people and what had happened on his own part. Thus the word admits both physical and spiritual ailment.

Then his Lord did not leave him in this open wasteland, after the whale had cast him onto this open land exhausted, and he was most like a child just after its birth. So God caused to grow over him a gourd plant, ﴿And We caused to grow over him a plant of gourd [yaqtin]﴾ [al-Saffat: 146]. It is a broad-leaved plant; they said it is the squash (gourd) plant, which shades and covers him and protects him from flies and insects, because he came out with secretions from the belly of the whale around him that impeded the breathing of his skin, impeded his health, and left him in a sticky, unwell state.

Therefore, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about the gourd plant, he said: "The pronoun in (ʿalayhi) refers to our master Yunus." This means that the growing of this plant occurred after the whale had cast him into the open land, and that the gourd plant had not been present in that place before.

So: the whale's swallowing of our master Yunus (peace be upon him) was a mercy from God to him, instead of his being lost in the vast sea, with the waves tossing him, and we do not know where they would carry him. As for the whale, it has a will, and it can keep him and cast him onto dry land. Thus we stand before a chain of God's mercies to Yunus (peace be upon him).

As for His saying, ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ and ﴿They believed, so We let them enjoy for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 147–148], it is as if the Truly Holy (al-Haqq) is saying to us: beware lest you think that what happened to Yunus impugns his mission, or makes us change our view of him as a messenger. He was sent to ﴿a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147], and the hundred thousand here may be a figure of speech for a large number, because the thousand was in ancient times the limit of what people knew of numbers.

Therefore, when they wished to ransom the daughter of Kisra (I think) when she fell into captivity, they offered to the one who had been allotted her share among the Muslims such-and-such thousand, and he agreed. His companions said to him after he had concluded this deal: Why did you not ask for more? They were able to ransom her with much more wealth. He said: By God, if I knew that beyond the thousand there was a number, I would have said it.

As for His saying, ﴿or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147], does the Truly Holy not know the exact number of these people? Yes, He knows them, may He be exalted, and had He wished He would have named them to us precisely. Rather, His saying ﴿or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147] is not to indicate increase, but to confirm the preceding number of a hundred thousand, as when you say "I gave so-and-so his right and more": you are not speaking of an increase, but emphasizing the number, and that it is not less, because "thousand" is also applied to what approaches a thousand, such as nine hundred and ninety-nine. Thus the "more" here affirms the completeness of the number.

As for His saying, ﴿So they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 148], since the enjoyment is limited by a time at which it ends, it is the enjoyment of this world. The enjoyment of this world for the believer ends in something better than it, so do not say: God ended the believer's enjoyment, because the cessation of worldly enjoyment connects you to the enjoyment of the Hereafter. Your enjoyment in this world is limited by your lifespan in it, and bounded by the limits of your capacities and abilities, whereas the enjoyment of the Hereafter remains and comes according to the capacities of the Bestower, may He be exalted.

Thus: this is an honour, that you are transferred from the bliss of this world to the bliss of the Hereafter, and His saying ﴿for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 148] is counted as a kindness from God.

After that, the Truly Holy turns to another matter:

﴿So ask them: "Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?..."﴾ [al-Saffat: 149].

Then his Lord did not leave him in this open wasteland, after the fish had cast him onto this barren land, exhausted and most like a newborn infant. So God caused a gourd plant to grow for him, as the Qur'an says: ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd plant of [broad] leaves﴾. It is a tree with broad leaves. They said: it is the gourd tree (al-qar'), which shades and covers him and protects him from flies and insects, because he came out with secretions from the fish's belly around him that hindered the breathing of his skin, affected his health, and left his temperament sticky...

The pronoun in (ʿalayhi, "over him") refers to our master Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him. This means that the growth of this tree occurred after the fish had cast him onto the open land, and the gourd tree had not been present in that place before.

So, the fish's swallowing of our master Yunus, peace be upon him, was a mercy from God to him, instead of his being lost in the vast sea, tossed about by the waves, with no knowing where they would carry him. As for the fish, it has its own will, and it can keep him and cast him onto the shore. Thus we are faced with a chain of God's mercies upon Yunus, peace be upon him.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is saying to us: beware lest you think that what happened with Yunus (Jonah) casts doubt on his mission, or leads us to change our view of him as a messenger. He was sent to a hundred thousand or more. The "hundred thousand" here may be a figurative expression (kinayah) for a large number, because in earlier times the thousand was the highest number people commonly knew.

As for His saying, "or more": does the Truth, glory be to Him, not know the exact number of these people? Yes, He knows them, glory be to Him, and had He wished to mention them precisely, He would have done so for us. His words "or more" are not meant to indicate an increase. Rather, they confirm the earlier number, a hundred thousand, just as one says, "I gave so-and-so his due and more." You are not speaking of an increase; you are emphasizing the number and that it is not less. For the word "thousand" is also used for what approaches a thousand, such as nine hundred and ninety-nine. Thus the "more" here affirms that the number is complete.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verses 149–152:

His saying: ﴿So ask their opinion﴾ [al-Saffat: 149]. The word istafta (to ask for a fatwa) means: to seek fatwa (fatya, a legal ruling), just as istakhraja means to seek extraction and istafhama means to seek understanding. The word fatya means the limit of strength, and from it come fata (young man) and futuwwa (chivalry). So the meaning of istafta is: to seek what strengthens one in the matter of ruling (fatwa). The one who does not know a religious matter, for example, asks about it and seeks a fatwa, meaning: having been weak in religion, he seeks to become strong in the affair of his religion. From this is the saying of the Exalted concerning our master Ibrahim: ﴿We heard a young man mention them, called Ibrahim﴾ [al-Anbiya': 60].

And concerning the People of the Cave: ﴿Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 13].

That is: they were not elders. It is remarkable that faith should come with the vigour and exuberance of youth, which is the seat of desires and appetites. Therefore the hadith states: ...

The Exalted has shown us in the measures of societies that they are not free of twelve kinds, six of them among the beloved and six among the hateful, and we seek refuge with Allah. Of the beloved are the beloved and the more beloved; and of the hateful likewise are the hateful and the more hateful.

The Exalted says in the hadith qudsi: these six who are beloved; and you can bring the counterparts to these, who are the hated, and we seek refuge with Allah.

So: the obedient young man is more beloved to Allah, because he has the incentives of desire, its justifications and its vigour, yet he overcomes them and walks the path of obedience. This is unlike the elder whose desire has departed and whose incentives have lessened. Likewise is the case of the generous rich man and the humble poor man.

These three represent the summit of advancement in societies and the summit of vicegerency on earth. Imagine a society whose youth are obedient, whose poor are generous, and whose rich are humble. Below this is the rank of a society whose elders are obedient, whose rich are generous and humble, and below these are the hateful, and we seek refuge with Allah.

So the meaning of ﴿So ask their opinion﴾ [al-Saffat: 149] is: ask of them the fatwa that strengthens you in your disputed matter. Therefore we say to the mufti whom people seek for a fatwa: people want you to strengthen them with your opinion, so do not lead them toward the wealthy, for by that you encourage them toward the wealthy; you are then not strengthening them but weakening them. Rather, give them the correct ruling, for it is the true strength.

But why does the Exalted command the Prophet to ask the people for an opinion? They said: because when a matter's ruling is known to the speaker, he says: "I do not judge in it; rather, my opponent is the one who judges." Why? Because you are certain that if he turns the question over in his mind he will find nothing but to say what you want, as you say to one who denies your favour: "I accept your judgment; did I not stand by you on such and such a day?" Thus it is posed as a question, because you are certain of the answer.

But if the statement comes from you as a declarative, the declarative admits both truth and falsehood. Therefore the Truth discusses this matter with this interrogative: ﴿Is it for your Lord that there are daughters, and for them sons?﴾ [al-Saffat: 149]. This interrogative carries the meaning of denunciation and wonder: that is, how do you say that? For they said: the angels are daughters of Allah, and then they attributed sons to Allah, the Exalted.

Therefore the Qur'an answers them: ﴿Is it for your Lord that there are daughters, and for them sons?﴾ [al-Saffat: 149]. How? Who created? It is Allah, the Creator of the male and the Creator of the female. So how do you choose for yourselves the better sex, namely males, and assign to Allah the daughters?

How, when one of you is given the good news of a female, his face remains darkened while he is anguished, hiding himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given good news of; then he considers: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?﴾ [al-Nahl: 59].

The word ﴿bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59] means alive, because paternal tenderness cannot bear that a father see his child die, or that he strangle it with his own hand; so he rids himself of it by burying it in the dust so that he does not see it.

In another verse the Exalted said: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face remains darkened and he is suppressed with grief. Is one who is brought up in ornament and is unclear in dispute [to be attributed to Allah]?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 17–18]. That is: do you attribute to Allah one who is reared in luxury and adornment, namely daughters, while you assign to yourselves sons, capable of work, striving and bearing hardships? Therefore the Exalted judged this division to be unjust and tyrannical.

So He said: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [al-Najm: 21–22]. Consider the word (ḍīzā): had it been outside the Qur'an it would be heavy and unpalatable, but it comes in its context as the speech of Allah, natural and smooth as spring water. Why? Because it is placed in its position to express this unjust and remarkable division, which no word but this remarkable word can express, with the cadence that rings in the ear.

Then the Truth, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ [al-Saffat: 150].

So: you are mistaken, indeed ignorant and stupid, in two matters. The first: that you made the angels females. The second: that you took the males for yourselves and left the daughters for Allah. Who told you the angels are daughters? The words "daughter" and "son" arise from marriage and procreation, and the angels neither marry nor procreate, and are not characterised by maleness or femaleness.

Moreover, whoever judges the angels to be females must have witnessed your creation, and Allah says: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19].

And in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor of themselves, and I would not take misleaders as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]. The Truth informs us of this reality: ﴿and I would not take misleaders as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51], that is: assistants and aides in the process of creation. He exposes those who come and speak about the matter of creation as if they had seen it, saying: the angels are females, and saying: man's origin is an ape, and so on through these claims.

The Truth warns us against them to give us the immunity necessary to confront them, and it suffices that we know this is an unseen matter of which they have no knowledge except what the Creator, the Exalted, has told us; yet He has left in the cosmos what demonstrates His truthfulness regarding what we did not witness.

The Exalted refutes these falsehoods by His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49]. Every kind among the kinds subsists in itself, and there is nothing that has evolved from something else. Likewise He said: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36].

As for the angels, they have a special nature unsuited to pairing, for they are characterised neither by maleness nor femaleness, just as they neither eat, drink, nor sleep, etc. And although this matter is contrary to reason, take it along with the other things contrary to reason, by which your faith in the unseen matters that your Lord has told you is tested; and the capital of these unseen matters that Allah has told you of is that you have believed in the One who speaks and informs of them.

Then the Truth, the Exalted, moves to another matter, saying: ﴿Unquestionably, it is from their own falsehood that they say: "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-Saffat: 151–152]. So their audacity against Allah did not stop at describing the angels as females, nor at attributing daughters to Allah, the Exalted; their audacity reached the very Essence of Allah, the Exalted, and they said: ﴿Allah has begotten﴾ [al-Saffat: 152].

It is as if the Truth, the Exalted, gives room to the obstinate and lets him loose until he says a word that exposes his lie, unmasks his claim, and shows that the obstinate one in matters of religion is a foolish dolt. For they said ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116], and now they say "Allah has begotten," and there is a great difference between the two statements: "Allah has begotten" attributes offspring to Allah directly, whereas "Allah has taken a son" means He did not beget but adopted a son, so the basis is that He has no son, hence He took one. Let us examine the matter of taking a son from our own reality: why do we seek a son and desire him? Why do we grieve when childbearing is withheld and become anxious when a son is delayed? They say: because the son is a memorial and an extension of his father; so a man rejoices in his son and rejoices even more in his grandson, for through a son he preserves his memory for one generation, and through a grandson for two generations. How strange is our situation with this world: how we cling to it and grasp at it even through memory; and if the world does not last for you, what benefit is the world of others?

When Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, spoke on this matter, when a grandson came to him and he rejoiced in him, he said:

So secure for yourself after your death its memory,
For remembrance is for a person a second life.

Therefore the Truth answers them: ﴿Had Allah desired to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He wills from what He creates﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. He is free of need from His creation, to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and all the servants are His handiwork and dependents, so He has no need of a support as you need.

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He has not taken a companion or a son﴾ [al-Jinn: 3], that is: He had no companion, that is, no wife from whom He would have a son. When a person makes a statement, this statement is called a verbal relation; if it is preceded by an existential relation that corresponds to the speech, the speech is truth; and if the relation is to a speech that has no reality, it is falsehood. So: you are mistaken, indeed ignorant and foolish, in two matters. The first: you have made the angels females. The second: you have taken the males for yourselves and left the daughters for God. Who told you that the angels are daughters? The word "daughter" and "son" arises from marriage and procreation, and the angels do not marry or procreate, nor are they characterized by maleness or femaleness.

Then, whoever judges the angels to be females must have witnessed your creation, and God says: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19].

The words ﴿and I would not take misguiders as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51] mean: aides and assistants in the process of creation. He exposes those who will come and speak about the matter of creation as if they had seen it, so they say: the angels are females, and they say: man's origin is a monkey, and so on through these claims.

The Truth warns us against them so as to give us the immunity needed to confront them. It is enough for us to know that this is an unseen matter of which they have no knowledge, except what the Creator, glorified be He, has told us. Nevertheless, He has left in the cosmos what demonstrates the truthfulness of His report concerning what we did not witness...

As for the angels, they have a special nature that is not suited to marriage, since they are characterized neither by maleness nor by femaleness, just as they do not eat, drink, or sleep, etc. Even if this matter is contrary to reason, take it as well among the matters contrary to reason by which your faith in the unseen things that your Lord has told you is tested. His saying: ﴿So ask their opinion﴾ [al-Saffat: 149]. The Exalted has shown us in the measures of societies that they are not free of twelve kinds, six of them among the beloved and six among the hateful, and we seek refuge with Allah. Of the beloved are the beloved and the more beloved; and of the hateful likewise are the hateful and the more hateful.

The Exalted says in the hadith qudsi: these six who are beloved; and you can bring the counterparts to these, who are the hated, and we seek refuge with Allah.

So: the obedient young man is more beloved to Allah, because he has the incentives of desire, its justifications and its vigour, yet he overcomes them and walks the path of obedience. This is unlike the elder whose desire has departed and whose incentives have lessened. Likewise is the case of the generous rich man and the humble poor man.

These three represent the summit of advancement in societies and the summit of vicegerency on earth. Imagine a society whose youth are obedient, whose poor are generous, and whose rich are humble. Below this is the rank of a society whose elders are obedient, whose rich are generous and humble, and below these are the hateful, and we seek refuge with Allah.

Rather, give them the correct ruling, for it is the true strength.

But why does the Exalted command the Prophet to ask the people for an opinion? They said: because when a matter's ruling is known to the speaker, he says: "I do not judge in it; rather, my opponent is the one who judges." Why? Because you are certain that if he turns the question over in his mind he will find nothing but to say what you want, as you say to one who denies your favour: "I accept your judgment; did I not stand by you on such and such a day?" How, when one of you is given the good news of a female, his face remains darkened while he is anguished, hiding himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given good news of; then he considers: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?﴾ [al-Nahl: 59].

The word ﴿bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59] means alive, because paternal tenderness cannot bear that a father see his child die, or that he strangle it with his own hand; so he rids himself of it by burying it in the dust so that he does not see it.

The hamza in ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ [al-Saffat: 153] is the hamza of interrogation (hamzat al-istifham), because the verb ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ [al-Saffat: 153] begins with a hamzat wasl (the connecting hamza). When the interrogative hamza entered upon it, the hamzat wasl was dropped and the hamza that carries the meaning of interrogation was retained, so its original form is: aʾistafa (أاصطفى). This interrogation is for amazement and denunciation, because Allah, glory be to Him, is the Creator of both sons and daughters. How, then, would He choose for Himself the lesser of the two sexes, when He is the Creator of both?

So this is a statement that is not accepted even by the measure of reason; the matter is clear. We have already explained that Allah, glory be to Him, asks them questions so that the judgment comes from them, by way of acknowledgment (iqrar) and not as mere report, and acknowledgment is the master of proofs, whereas a report admits of both truth and falsehood, in the intellect.

This is a rational proof that refutes this claim. However, rational proof may differ among minds, so Allah, glory be to Him, moves us to the transmitted proof, perhaps they have a book they study on this matter:

The word ﴿sultan﴾ [As-Saffat: 156] is either a sultan of proof that convinces, or a sultan of force and compulsion. The difference between them is that the sultan of proof persuades the other party so that he acts willingly, whereas the sultan of force compels him so that he acts unwillingly. The meaning is: you have neither a sultan of proof nor of compulsion.

Similar to this is His saying, relating from Iblis on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. That is, I have no power by which I can force you to obey me, nor any proof by which I can convince you; rather, you were yourselves ready (tashwirah), meaning, prepared for misguidance and disobedience.

The meaning of ﴿mubin﴾ [As-Saffat: 156] is clear and evident.

His saying, ﴿So bring your Book, if you are truthful﴾ [As-Saffat: 157], means: if you have any authority, then bring your Book, that is, the one revealed to you from Allah that informs you of this.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verses 158–159:

The word (al-Jinna) with a kasra, and likewise al-Janna with a fatha, and from the same root come al-Jinn and majnun (possessed/mad). All of them derive from the root (j-n-n), which conveys concealment and covering. Here (al-Jinna) means the angels. They were so named because they are hidden from us, so we do not see them. Likewise al-Janna (the Garden) is so named because it covers whoever walks in it with the abundance of its trees, or covers whoever is in it by providing all his needs, so that he has no need to leave it. Likewise the majnun (the one afflicted with madness) is so named because his intellect has disappeared and become hidden.

The meaning is that they (the polytheists) made a kinship between Allah, exalted is He, and the angels when they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿And indeed, the Jinna have known that they will surely be brought forth (for punishment)﴾ [al-Saffat: 158]. That is: the angels knew that these polytheists who associate partners with Allah will be brought forth for punishment. Muhdar (brought forth) is a passive participle, meaning: they will be compelled to attend.

Then Allah refutes them, declaring Himself free of any resemblance to creation: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾ [al-Saffat: 159]. The phrase (Subhan Allah) we see always in every context; it removes the Essence from resemblance to creation. The quality of tasbih (glorifying) belonging to Allah, that is, the declaration of His transcendence, exists and is established for Allah, exalted is He, before the one who glorifies comes into existence.

Thus the word (Subhan) means absolute transcendence of Allah before He created anyone who would glorify Him. When Allah created creation, it glorified Him: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Hashr: 1]. And He said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ [al-Taghabun: 1]. That is: it continues to glorify Him in the present and in the future until the Hour is established.

Since this quality of tasbih is established for Allah, exalted is He, before creation and after it, and it endures in the past, present and future, then, O most noble and honoured of creation, for whose sake all creation was made, beware lest you fail to glorify Him or deviate from this glorifying order: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1]. So the meaning of ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾ [al-Saffat: 159] is: the Truth, exalted is He, is far removed from the words of these polytheists and their lies, and He is exalted above having any kinship between Himself and the Jinna.

Commentary on the relation (munasabah) of His saying, "Except the sincere servants of Allah" (Q. 37:160), as an exception from His saying, "Indeed, they will be brought forth [to punishment]" (Q. 37:158). So Allah excepted His sincere servants from entering with those brought forth to punishment.

And His saying, "Indeed, you and what you worship" (Q. 37:161), i.e., besides Allah, "are not able to lead astray" (Q. 37:162), meaning: you and what you worship besides Allah will not cause My creation to turn against Me. That is, you will not corrupt creation against Allah, the Exalted. It is said: "Fatana fulan 'ala fulan zawjatahu" (so-and-so turned his wife against so-and-so), meaning he corrupted her against him. The meaning is: you are not able to corrupt [the relationship] between Me and My angels.

And how could they, when the angels themselves were created only for My worship and love, "They glorify [Him] night and day; they never tire" (Q. 21:20)? How could you corrupt them when they are innocent of you and of your worship of them, and even curse you? So how could you corrupt them against Allah?

In another place, the Exalted responds to them: "Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord, [striving as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy..." (Q. 17:57). Meaning: those whom they worship besides Allah themselves seek to Allah the means (wasilah) that brings them near to Him.

And in another place He said: "Say, 'If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne'" (Q. 17:42).

So: you are not able to lead astray these worshipped ones from their Lord, because they have made worship sincerely for Allah and they compete in drawing near to Him.

As for His saying, "Except one who will burn in Hellfire" (Q. 37:163), meaning: except whoever among mankind is pleased with servitude [to others than Allah], his destination is the Fire. Therefore, when He, glorified be He, wished to rebuke those who worshipped stones, He said: "Look, you will not be punished in the Fire except by stones, so that you may see your deity with you and like you in the Fire." If it is said: what is the sin of these stones that were worshipped besides Allah?

He, glorified be He, says:

"And there is none of us except that he has a known station" (Q. 37:164)...

Therefore: these stones, when they are heated to torment these polytheists with them, are not so because they have any sin for which they are punished. Rather, they have a known station and a commitment to carrying out God's command against the one who opposes Him: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Saffat: 164].

That is: a measure and a rank. The angels are degrees and ranks; the lower does not harbor resentment toward the higher, nor does the higher look down on the lower, because the known station in which God placed them is a measure set by God Almighty, and they respect the measure of God in the creation of God. This is a lesson we ought to learn: that each of us should observe the worth and standing of others. When I respect the one who is above me, I am in fact respecting the measure of God, who made him above me, even if he was beneath me on some day. We have said that the universe is not a matter of (mechanics) but a creation with a measure and with wisdom willed by God.

So how can we be daughters of God? And how can we be worshipped besides God, when we are subjected to worship Him, glory be to Him, and we are soldiers arranged in rows, awaiting His commands, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks﴾ [al-Saffat: 165]. That is: we stand in orderly rows, and the row is the proof of order and the emblem of commitment and discipline. Therefore it has been reported in the hadith: "Why? Because you stand before God, glory be to Him, so show God from yourselves what indicates equality, commitment and solidarity."

And in war likewise: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾ [al-Saff: 4]. This simile has its significance, for a solid structure means that no brick in it has the will to depart from the others, since it is governed by the building into which it has been placed. Therefore, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reviewed the rows in one of the campaigns, he saw a soldier who had strayed from his row, so he gestured to him with his staff that he should align himself with his fellows and keep discipline in his row.

Then they say: ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [God]﴾ [al-Saffat: 166], meaning: how could we accept to be worshipped besides God, when we were created only to glorify Him, Exalted is He:

﴿And indeed, they used to say, "If only we had a reminder..."﴾

How can we be daughters of God? And how could we be worshipped instead of God, when we are subjugated to His worship, Glory be to Him, and we are soldiers arrayed in rows, awaiting His commands, exalted is He? ﴿And indeed, we are the ones who stand in ranks﴾. That is: we stand in orderly rows. The row (al-saff) is a sign of order and a mark of commitment and discipline. Therefore, it has been reported in a hadith: "Indeed, Allah does not look at a crooked row." Why? Because you stand before Allah, Glory be to Him, so show Allah from yourselves that which indicates equality, commitment and unity.

﴿And indeed, they used to say, "If only we had a reminder..."﴾

Their saying: ﴿If only we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾ [al-Saffat: 168], that is, a book and a revealed scripture ﴿from the former peoples﴾ [al-Saffat: 168], like what was sent down to the earlier messengers, ﴿we would surely have been sincere servants of Allah﴾ [al-Saffat: 169]. It is strange of them that they justify their polytheism with this argument, when the master of all the messengers has come to them. The earlier messengers had limited missions in time and place, and all of them, before the Messenger of Allah, were charged with conveying the command of Allah to creation. As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he is the only messenger who was empowered by Allah to legislate for creation, because his mission is general in time and in place until the Hour.

So: how can you want a reminder from the former peoples when with you is the Seal of the Messengers, the legislator, to whom the universal matter comes from Allah, so that he clarifies it, explains it and details it?

As for His saying: ﴿So they disbelieved in it﴾ [al-Saffat: 170], it means: when the messenger they had been asking for came to them, they disbelieved in him. So the matter is one of obstinacy, stubbornness and arrogance in accepting the truth and submitting to it. ﴿But they will soon know﴾ [al-Saffat: 170]. The two particles (al-sin) and (sawfa) both indicate the future, but sawfa is further away in time than al-sin.

Thus His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿But they will soon know﴾ [al-Saffat: 170] is a temporal precaution from the Noble Qur'an. The verb ﴿they know﴾ [al-Saffat: 170] is present, referring to both the present and the future, but sawfa refers to a distant future beyond the future of al-sin. This is because among those contemporary with the revelation of the Qur'an there were those who would die before they saw the outcome of the polytheists, and before they witnessed the rise of Islam and its victories.

If someone died before he came to know, then he will know in the Hereafter and see the outcome. This applies to the non-believer. As for the believer, he has no need of this knowledge, because he has believed Allah in what He informed of. Among this is the saying of Imam ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him: "Were the veil removed from me, I would not increase in certainty."

Therefore, when the saying of Allah, Exalted is He, was revealed—and the Muslims were in distress, hardship and constraint before the conquest—﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45], and the particle sin indicates the near future, Sayyidina ʿUmar was astonished, and what would make you know what ʿUmar is. The Qur'an was descending according to what he was seeing, yet he was astonished and said: "What host is this, when we are unable to protect ourselves and our families?" Then when the conquest came, the Muslims were victorious and what happened happened, he said: "Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]."

The believer, then, affirms what Allah has informed of, because it is a matter decreed eternally in the knowledge of Allah. Since it has already been decreed in eternity, and there is no opposing force that can overturn what Allah has decreed, and since Allah, Exalted is He, is not subject to any incapacity that would prevent Him from executing what He has decreed, it is certainly going to happen.

We say: the one speaking these words is Allah, not us, and Allah is not bound by time. When He informs of a matter, it is happening, because there is no repeller of what He has decreed eternally. So the command of Allah came eternally, therefore do not hasten it as something happening.

That is because some of those contemporary with the revelation of the Qur'an would die before seeing the end of the polytheists, and before witnessing the rise of Islam and its victories.

So if he dies before he comes to know, then he will come to know in the Hereafter and see the outcome. This applies to the non-believer. As for the believer, he has no need of this knowledge, because he has believed God in what He informed..."

Note on the verse: the passage comments on ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ (37:171), "And certainly Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers."

The meaning of "sabaqat kalimatuna" (سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا, "Our word has preceded"): it means: We said it before the whole of creation. This word has synonyms: "sabaqat kalimatuna," "waqa'at," and "haqqat." "Sabaqat" means: by its determination before occurrence. "Waqa'at" means: it fell at the moment of occurrence. "Haqqat" means: it is a truth that I decree by My power, and a truth that it should befall whom I will. Therefore: these are meanings that converge together and complement one another.

What is this word that preceded from God to His servants, the messengers? It is His saying: ﴿Indeed, they will surely be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers will surely be the dominant.﴾

These are two matters: the messengers will inevitably be victorious, and the (divine) soldiers will inevitably prevail. This is a word that preceded from God and a decree that cannot be reversed. Therefore the scholars and the people of knowledge have taken from these verses that soldiership (jundiyyah, here meaning service as God's soldiers) has conditions. Whoever fulfils them deserves victory, and whoever falls short of them deserves defeat.

So when we look at the outcome of a battle between Muslims and disbelievers, if the Muslims are victorious, know that they fulfilled the conditions of soldiership to God. If they are defeated, they should look into themselves, seek the causes of the failure, and examine the point of their violation of the law of soldiership, for if they had remained steadfast in their soldiership to God, God's promise of victory would have been realized for them.

This matter is clear in the battles of Badr and Uhud. At Badr the Muslims were victorious because they did not violate the law of soldiership to God, the Exalted. But at Uhud they were not victorious, although the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among them. Do not be surprised at this, for it is a natural matter. Did they not disobey the command of the Messenger of God? Indeed they did. So how would it have been if they had been victorious despite this disobedience? By God, if God had granted them victory, the command of the Messenger of God would have become insignificant to them afterwards, and they would have said: "We disobeyed him on such-and-such a day and we were victorious." Thus the outcome at Uhud was that the disobedient, failing Muslims were defeated, but Islam was victorious, and its laws and principles were exalted.

As for the messengers, they are certain of God's promise of victory to them, and this is a matter that is not debated among them. The evidence for this is from the story of our master Moses (peace be upon him). When he went out of Egypt with the Children of Israel, Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued him, until they nearly overtook him at the shore of the sea, and the people of Moses said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken.﴾

So how did our master Moses respond? (He said: "No!") With full conviction he denies a reality that could occur in a single moment: the sea is in front of them and the enemy behind them. Yet he says: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾

This is the certainty in the words ﴿Indeed, they will surely be the victorious﴾, that is, the messengers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 37, verse 173:

The meaning of ﴿Our word had already preceded﴾ [al-Saffat: 171] is: We said it before the whole creation. This word has synonyms: "Our word preceded," "occurred," and "became binding." "Preceded" means: it was determined before it came into being; "occurred" means at the moment of its coming into being; and "became binding" means: it is binding that I decree by My power, and binding that it befall whomever I will. So these are meanings that converge together and complete one another.

What, then, is this word that preceded from Allah concerning His messengers? It is His saying: ﴿Indeed, they will surely be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will surely be the overcoming﴾ [al-Saffat: 172-173].

These are two matters: the messengers are without doubt victorious, and the soldiers are without doubt overcoming. This is a word that preceded from Allah, a decree that cannot be turned back. Therefore the scholars and people of knowledge have taken from these verses that soldiership (al-jundiyyah) has conditions: whoever fulfils them deserves victory, and whoever falls short of them deserves defeat.

So when we look at the outcome of a battle between Muslims and disbelievers, if the Muslims are victorious, know that they have fulfilled the conditions of soldiership to Allah; and if they are defeated, then they must look into themselves, seek out the causes of the flaw and the point of their violation of the law of soldiership; for if they had remained steadfast in their soldiership to Allah, the promise of Allah's victory would have been realised for them.

This matter is clear in the battle of Badr and in Uhud. At Badr the Muslims were victorious because they did not violate the law of soldiership to Allah, the Exalted. But at Uhud they were not victorious, although the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them. Do not be surprised at that, for this is a natural matter. Did they not disobey the command of the Messenger of Allah? Indeed they did. So how would it be if they had been victorious despite this disobedience? By Allah, if Allah had granted them victory, the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have become insignificant to them afterwards, and they would have said: "We disobeyed him on such-and-such a day and we were victorious." So the outcome: on the day of Uhud, the slackening Muslims were defeated, but Islam was victorious and its laws and principles were exalted.

As for the messengers, they are confident in Allah's promise of victory to them, and this is a matter among them that is not debated. The evidence for this is from the story of our master Musa (peace be upon him). When he left Egypt with the Children of Israel, Pharaoh and his armies followed them, until they nearly overtook him at the shore of the sea, and even the people of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are to be overtaken﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 61].

So what did our master Musa reply? He said, "No!" – with full certainty, denying a reality that could occur a single moment later: the sea was before them and the enemy behind them. Yet he said: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 62].

This is the confidence in the saying ﴿Indeed, they will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 172], meaning the messengers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 37, verse 174:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So turn away from them﴾.

That is: leave them now in their falsehood and turn away from them. Why, when the Truth, glorified is He, is able to grant victory to His religion from its very beginning, in an instant? They said: the Truth, glorified is He, wills that falsehood spread and rise high, until it bites people, so they come to hate it and feel constricted by it.

And also, so that the people of truth may be trained in trials and hardships, and their fiber may grow strong. ﴿And watch them, for they will see﴾. Meaning: look at their state and the outcome of their affair, and they will see this outcome themselves.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 37, verses 175–177:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So turn away from them﴾ [al-Saffat: 174].

That is: leave them now in their falsehood and turn away from them. Why, when Allah, glory be to Him, is able to grant victory to His religion from its very beginning in an instant? They said: Allah, glory be to Him, wants falsehood to spread and to rise high until it bites people, so that they come to hate it and feel constricted by it.

Also, so that the people of truth may be trained in trials and hardships, and their resolve may grow firm. ﴿And watch them, for they will [soon] see﴾ [al-Saffat: 175]: that is, look at their state and the outcome of their affair, and they will see this outcome themselves, and the punishment that will befall them, the punishment they are hastening for: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [al-Saffat: 176].

As He, the Exalted, said in another place: ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 22].

This is their folly, because this punishment, which they deny and consider far-fetched, is certain to come: ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned﴾ [al-Saffat: 177]. The sahah (courtyard) is the wide place or open space in which people find room to breathe and an outlet that relieves them. And ﴿descends﴾ [al-Saffat: 177] means: it alights, befalls, and surprises them.

﴿Evil will be the morning of those who were warned﴾ [al-Saffat: 177]: that is, this morning is wretched and evil. The morning is the appointed true time for battle, to surprise the combatant before he is prepared; or the punishment will overtake them in broad daylight, so that they cannot hide from the disgrace. And ﴿those who were warned﴾ [al-Saffat: 177] are the people whom We warned and cautioned.

And ﴿those who were warned﴾ [al-Saffat: 177] are the people whom We warned and cautioned.

The Almighty's saying in the previous verse: ﴿So turn away from them for a time﴾ refers to the time of this world. Likewise, ﴿and see them﴾ means in this world, and ﴿they will see﴾ means in this world. This "time" is the one Allah referred to when He said: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾ [Ghafir: 77], meaning some of the punishment in this world, ﴿or We take you in death, and to Us they will return﴾ [Ghafir: 77], meaning in the Hereafter.

As for the "time" here, in ﴿So turn away from them for a time﴾, it refers to the time of the Hereafter. It is not a repetition of the first "time." Likewise, ﴿and see﴾ and ﴿they will see﴾ refer to the Hereafter, when the punishment they denied and rejected suddenly confronts them. Then they will say at that moment: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾ [As-Sajdah: 12].

"His saying in the previous verse, ﴿So turn away from them for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 174], refers to the time of this world. Likewise, ﴿and watch them﴾ [al-Saffat: 175], meaning: in this world, ﴿for they will see﴾ [al-Saffat: 175], meaning: in this world. And this 'time' is the one about which Allah said: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We threaten them with﴾ [Ghafir: 77], meaning: some of the punishment in this world, ﴿or cause you to die, then to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77], in the Hereafter.

As for the 'time' here, ﴿and turn away from them for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 178], it refers to the time of the Hereafter, so it is not a repetition of the first 'time.' Likewise, ﴿and watch, and they will see﴾ [al-Saffat: 179] refers to the Hereafter, when the punishment they denied and disbelieved in suddenly confronts them, and they will say at that time: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12]."

Al-Sha'rawi concludes the surah with the "subhaniyyah" (the declaration of God's transcendence), which affirms God's absolute tanzih (freedom from likeness and deficiency) in His essence, which is unlike any essence; in His attributes, which are unlike any attributes; and in His acts, which are unlike any acts. Everything that belongs to Him, and everything in creation that bears a relation to it, is to be understood within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

So the meaning of ﴿Glory be to your Lord﴾ is: your Lord is exalted above every deficiency and above every resemblance. Created beings have essences, but not like His essence; they have existence, but not like His existence; they have independence (ghina), but not like His independence; and they have wisdom, but not like His wisdom... etc.

As for ﴿Lord of Majesty﴾ (Rabb al-'Izzah): the word "Rabb" carries the sense of tarbiyah (upbringing, cultivation), which is the qualifying of the one who nurtures, for he succeeds in the purpose entrusted to him and required of him. In order to prepare something, you must first know the purpose for which it was brought into existence; after that, you must have wisdom that determines for it the method that leads it to this purpose.

So then: who determines the purpose of human existence? We have said that the human maker is the one who determines the purpose of his creation first, before he begins making it. Does the inventor of television, for example, make it and then tell us: "Look for what this device can be used for"? No, rather he defines the goal and the purpose first. Likewise, your purpose, O human, is determined for you only by the One who created you. The maintenance of a creation is carried out by its maker; likewise, the upkeep of creation can only be by the method of the Truth.

Therefore we say: the world has not become corrupt except when man stepped outside this frame, defined his own purpose for himself, set for himself a way of life, and pushed his Maker and his Maker's method aside. We have said that the Creator's method for creation is like the "manual" (the catalogue) by which the creation is maintained and by which its defects are repaired. The one who sets out such a method must possess such precision and wisdom that nothing escapes it and nothing needs correcting, so that we are never obliged to amend what has been laid down. The Creator, glory be to Him, is the most knowledgeable of His servants and His creation, and He is the most knowledgeable of what benefits them in this world and in the next:

﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

Otherwise, why would the Creator summon us five times a day and night, and make the prayers an obligatory duty that never falls from a person under any circumstances? For this reason the prayer of travel and the prayer of the sick were legislated, so that if illness becomes severe, he prays even with the blink of an eye or with the movement of his heart.

We have said before on this matter: when you wish, for example, to meet a president or a senior official, you need an appointment in advance, approval and procedures; indeed, what you are to say is specified for you, and it is he who ends the meeting... etc. But your meeting with your Lord is the meeting of one who loves, who leaves it to his Beloved to determine the time, place and subject of the meeting, and leaves it to Him to end it whenever He wishes and to begin it whenever He wills. So if you want to meet your Lord, all you need do is prepare yourself for it and say: "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) — a word that places you directly in the presence of your Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Imagine a creation presented to its maker five times every day: would any defect or corruption remain in it? Therefore, "when a matter distressed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he would hasten to prayer, and he would say: 'Give us rest through it, O Bilal.'" Yes, give us rest through it, not rest from it.

So then: He, glory be to Him, mentioned at the conclusion the subhaniyyah, then the rububiyyah that nurtures you and prepares you for the task intended for you. This nurturing trains you for what? It trains you for 'izzah (might). ﴿Lord of Majesty﴾, and 'izzah means that you prevail and no one ever prevails over you. We have said — and to God belongs the highest likeness — that a small child who walks the street alone is dared by others, who harass and strike him; but if he walks in the company of his father and holds his hand, no one dares to approach him. Likewise, O Muslim, always be in the embrace of your Lord, in His hand, and in His company, and then no one will dare against you.

So then: the 'izzah with which God, glory be to Him, is characterized, and which He bestows upon His servants, is the dominance that cannot be overcome and the power that needs no one. There is another 'izzah, the 'izzah of sin, of which God said: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear God," pride seizes him for sin. Hell will suffice him; and wretched is the resting place﴾ [al-Baqarah: 206]. So the 'izzah here is arrogance without substance or support...

And peace be upon the messengers. That is: all of them together. For although they may at times have laid upon us what is hard on the soul, they have taken us by the hand to the shore of safety and deliverance. So upon them is peace from us whenever we mention them, we send blessings and greetings upon them.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds ﴿وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾, who guided us to follow the method through the messengers, and helped us to follow it. Praise be to Allah for the reward He has prepared for us of His bounty and His gardens in the Hereafter. For this reason, He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And the last of their call will be: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10].
